spreads.name: One card
spreads.for: Card of the day, a quick answer, a theme to carry, a meditation.
spreads.how: Hold the question (or simply the day) in mind, shuffle until it feels done, cut with the left hand and turn the top card.

positions.label: The card
positions.meaning: The energy of the day, the heart of the answer, the thing to notice.

spreads.read: Read the card whole: picture first, then meaning, then the question it raises. Drawn reversed, read it as the same energy blocked, turned inward or in excess. Write it down and look back at night.

spreads.name: Three cards
spreads.for: Almost anything; the most useful small spread.
spreads.tradition: Universal; the line of three is the oldest shape of a card sentence.
spreads.how: Deal three cards left to right.

positions.label: Past
positions.meaning: What led here; the root.

positions.label: Present
positions.meaning: Where things stand now.

positions.label: Future
positions.meaning: Where it is heading if nothing changes.

spreads.read: Read it as one sentence. Notice whether the cards face toward or away from each other, which suits and numbers repeat, and whether the middle card sits between friendly or hostile elements on either side.

spreads.name: The French cross
spreads.for: A clear question with a for and an against; the classic Marseille reading with majors only.
spreads.tradition: The tirage en croix of French cartomancy, usually with the 22 trumps alone.
spreads.how: Use the 22 majors only. Deal four: left, right, top, bottom. The fifth (the synthesis) is not dealt but counted: add the numbers of the four cards (the Fool counts 0 or 22, decide first); if the sum is over 22, add its digits; the card with that number goes in the centre.

positions.label: For
positions.meaning: What supports you: the yes of the matter.

positions.label: Against
positions.meaning: What opposes you: the no of the matter.

positions.label: The judge
positions.meaning: How to weigh it; what decides; the discussion.

positions.label: The result
positions.meaning: Where it ends.

positions.label: The synthesis
positions.meaning: The hidden key that joins the four, found by counting, not chance.

spreads.read: The synthesis card is the soul of the reading: if it repeats one of the four, that card is doubly important. If it is the Fool, the matter is open.

spreads.name: The elemental cross
spreads.for: Seeing yourself or a situation through the four elements and spirit; balance.
spreads.tradition: Built on the four suits and the quintessence.
spreads.how: Deal the centre first, then fire, water, air and earth around it.

positions.label: Spirit
positions.meaning: The heart, the self, what binds the four.

positions.label: Fire
positions.meaning: Will, drive, desire: what moves you.

positions.label: Water
positions.meaning: Feeling, love, intuition: what you feel.

positions.label: Air
positions.meaning: Thought, words, conflict: what you think.

positions.label: Earth
positions.meaning: Body, money, work, home: what is real.

spreads.read: A card whose suit matches its place is strong there; a card of the opposite element (fire in water, air in earth) shows the strain in that area.

spreads.name: The Celtic Cross
spreads.for: A detailed question; the whole shape of a situation, its roots and its likely end.
spreads.tradition: Published in London in 1911 as "an ancient Celtic method", now the most used spread in the world. Positions below follow that first published version; modern names in brackets.
spreads.how: Choose a significator (a court card for the person, or a card for the matter) and lay it face up. Shuffle, cut three times. Cover the significator with card 1, lay 2 across it, then 3 above, 4 below, 5 behind (the side the significator faces away from), 6 before (the side it faces). Cards 7 to 10 go in a column on the right, from the bottom up.

positions.label: What covers you (the present)
positions.meaning: The influence over the whole matter, the atmosphere everything else moves in.

positions.label: What crosses you (the challenge)
positions.meaning: The obstacle or the force working across the matter. Even a good card here is a help that doesn't help in this case. Always read upright.

positions.label: What crowns you (the aim)
positions.meaning: The ideal or goal, the best that can come of it, not yet real.

positions.label: What is beneath you (the root)
positions.meaning: The foundation, what has already happened and become yours.

positions.label: What is behind you (the recent past)
positions.meaning: The influence just passed or passing away.

positions.label: What is before you (the near future)
positions.meaning: The influence coming into action soon.

positions.label: Yourself
positions.meaning: Your position and attitude in the matter.

positions.label: Your house (others)
positions.meaning: The environment: people around you, your place in life, outside influences.

positions.label: Hopes and fears
positions.meaning: What you hope for and what you dread; often the same card read both ways.

positions.label: What will come (the outcome)
positions.meaning: The result, gathering everything else on the table.

spreads.read: Read the cross as time (5 past, 1 present, 6 future) and as depth (4 root, 1 present, 3 aim). Compare 3 and 10: is the aim reached? Compare 4 and 9: do the roots feed the fear? If card 10 is a court card, the matter ends up in that person's hands; lay the spread again with that court as significator. If card 10 is unclear, lay the spread again with card 10 as the significator. Many readers drop the significator and read card 1 as the person.

spreads.name: The horseshoe
spreads.for: A practical question that needs advice; a gentler alternative to the Celtic Cross.
spreads.tradition: Common nineteenth and twentieth century card-reading layout; also used with playing cards.
spreads.how: Deal seven cards in a V or a horseshoe, opening upward, left to right.

positions.label: The past
positions.meaning: What brought you here.

positions.label: The present
positions.meaning: Where you stand.

positions.label: Hidden influences
positions.meaning: What you can't see yet.

positions.label: Obstacles
positions.meaning: What stands in the way.

positions.label: The others
positions.meaning: The people and forces around you.

positions.label: What to do
positions.meaning: The best course of action.

positions.label: The outcome
positions.meaning: Where it leads if you follow 6.

spreads.read: The bottom card (4) is the turning point. Read the two arms against each other: 1 against 7, 2 against 6, 3 against 5.

spreads.name: The bond
spreads.for: Any relationship: lovers, friends, family, partners in work.
spreads.how: Deal 1 and 2 side by side, 3 between and below them, then 4 and 5 under 1 and 2, then 6 and 7 at the bottom.

positions.label: You
positions.meaning: How you are in this bond.

positions.label: Them
positions.meaning: How they are in this bond.

positions.label: The bond
positions.meaning: What is between you; the relationship as its own living thing.

positions.label: What you bring
positions.meaning: Your gift and your baggage.

positions.label: What they bring
positions.meaning: Their gift and their baggage.

positions.label: The challenge
positions.meaning: What strains the bond.

positions.label: The potential
positions.meaning: What it can become.

spreads.read: Compare 1 with 2 and 4 with 5 by element: friendly elements meet easily, opposed ones (fire and water, air and earth) rub. A reading about someone not present is about your bond with them, not a window into their private life.

spreads.name: Two paths
spreads.how: Deal 1 in the centre at the bottom, then path A up the left (2, 3, 4) and path B up the right (5, 6, 7).

positions.label: The question
positions.meaning: Where you stand as you choose.

positions.label: Path A: what it gives
positions.meaning: The gift of the first option.

positions.label: Path A: what it costs
positions.meaning: The price of the first option.

positions.label: Path A: where it leads
positions.meaning: The likely end of the first option.

positions.label: Path B: what it gives
positions.meaning: The gift of the second option.

positions.label: Path B: what it costs
positions.meaning: The price of the second option.

positions.label: Path B: where it leads
positions.meaning: The likely end of the second option.

spreads.read: Look first at which column has more majors (more fate in it) and which has more of your own suit. The cards don't choose for you; they show the shape of each road.

spreads.name: The twelve houses
spreads.for: A whole-life reading; seeing which area of life a question really lives in.
spreads.tradition: The astrological wheel, laid out with cards.
spreads.how: Deal twelve cards counterclockwise starting at the nine o'clock position (the first house, the ascendant), then one in the centre.

positions.label: First house
positions.meaning: The self, appearance, how you meet the world, new starts.

positions.label: Second house
positions.meaning: Money, possessions, values, self-worth.

positions.label: Third house
positions.meaning: Siblings, neighbours, messages, short trips, the everyday mind.

positions.label: Fourth house
positions.meaning: Home, family, roots, the end of things.

positions.label: Fifth house
positions.meaning: Pleasure, romance, creativity, play, children.

positions.label: Sixth house
positions.meaning: Daily work, routines, service, habits, pets.

positions.label: Seventh house
positions.meaning: Partners, marriage, contracts, open rivals.

positions.label: Eighth house
positions.meaning: Shared money, intimacy, inheritance, the occult, transformation.

positions.label: Ninth house
positions.meaning: Travel, study, belief, philosophy, the far horizon.

positions.label: Tenth house
positions.meaning: Career, reputation, ambition, your place in the world.

positions.label: Eleventh house
positions.meaning: Friends, groups, hopes and wishes.

positions.label: Twelfth house
positions.meaning: The hidden, secrets, retreat, the inner life, what undoes or frees you.

positions.label: The heart
positions.meaning: The theme over the whole wheel.

spreads.read: Look for the houses that drew majors: those areas carry the most weight now. A card in a house that shares its element (fire signs 1, 5, 9; earth 2, 6, 10; air 3, 7, 11; water 4, 8, 12) is at home there.

spreads.name: The year ahead
spreads.for: New year, a birthday, an equinox: a card for each coming month.
spreads.tradition: The houses wheel turned into a calendar.
spreads.how: Deal twelve cards around the circle like a clock face starting at one o'clock, one for each month from the next one, then one in the centre for the year as a whole.

positions.label: Month one
positions.meaning: The first month.

positions.label: Month two
positions.meaning: The second month.

positions.label: Month three
positions.meaning: The third month.

positions.label: Month four
positions.meaning: The fourth month.

positions.label: Month five
positions.meaning: The fifth month.

positions.label: Month six
positions.meaning: The sixth month.

positions.label: Month seven
positions.meaning: The seventh month.

positions.label: Month eight
positions.meaning: The eighth month.

positions.label: Month nine
positions.meaning: The ninth month.

positions.label: Month ten
positions.meaning: The tenth month.

positions.label: Month eleven
positions.meaning: The eleventh month.

positions.label: Month twelve
positions.meaning: The twelfth month.

positions.label: The year
positions.meaning: The theme of the whole year.

spreads.read: Keep the spread in a journal and read each month's card again when the month arrives. The year card can be checked against the year card worked out from the birthday (see the methods).

spreads.name: The Tree of Life
spreads.for: A deep reading of a person or a spiritual question; ten spheres from the highest aim down to daily life.
spreads.tradition: The Hermetic Qabalah: each card falls on one of the ten spheres.
spreads.how: Deal in the order of the lightning flash, from the crown down: 1 at the top, 2 right, 3 left, 4 right, 5 left, 6 centre, 7 right, 8 left, 9 centre, 10 at the root. The right column is the pillar of mercy, the left the pillar of severity.

positions.label: Kether, the crown
positions.meaning: The highest aim; spiritual purpose; what the question is really for.

positions.label: Chokmah, wisdom
positions.meaning: The creative force; drive; the spark and the father.

positions.label: Binah, understanding
positions.meaning: Form, limits, sorrow, patience; the mother; what gives shape.

positions.label: Chesed, mercy
positions.meaning: What is given; growth, generosity, gains, help.

positions.label: Geburah, severity
positions.meaning: What must be cut or fought; strength, conflict, discipline.

positions.label: Tiphareth, beauty
positions.meaning: The heart; the true self at the centre; what harmonises.

positions.label: Netzach, victory
positions.meaning: Desire, love, the feelings, the arts; what you long for.

positions.label: Hod, splendour
positions.meaning: The mind, words, learning, method; what you think.

positions.label: Yesod, foundation
positions.meaning: The deep mind, dreams, instinct, the moon; what lies underneath.

positions.label: Malkuth, the kingdom
positions.meaning: The body, home, money; the outcome in the real world.

spreads.read: Read the three pillars as three columns (mercy, balance, severity) and the tree in three layers (the top three as spirit, the middle six as the soul, the root as the world). A card whose number matches its sphere (an Ace on Kether, a Six on Tiphareth) is especially strong there.

spreads.name: The seven planets
spreads.for: A week ahead (one card a day, Sunday to Saturday) or the seven powers in your life.
spreads.tradition: The seven classical planets and their days.
spreads.how: Deal seven cards in a circle, starting at the top and going clockwise in the order of the week.

positions.label: Sun (Sunday)
positions.meaning: The self, vitality, success, being seen.

positions.label: Moon (Monday)
positions.meaning: Feelings, home, dreams, the tides of the week.

positions.label: Mars (Tuesday)
positions.meaning: Drive, conflict, courage, what you fight for.

positions.label: Mercury (Wednesday)
positions.meaning: Thought, messages, travel, trade.

positions.label: Jupiter (Thursday)
positions.meaning: Luck, growth, generosity, wisdom.

positions.label: Venus (Friday)
positions.meaning: Love, pleasure, beauty, friends.

positions.label: Saturn (Saturday)
positions.meaning: Limits, duty, time, the lesson.

spreads.read: As a week, turn each day's card at breakfast and read it again at night. As powers, compare each card with the planet that rules it in the correspondences (a Mars card in the Mars place is doubled).

spreads.name: New moon
spreads.for: The dark of the moon: planting intentions.
spreads.tradition: Modern moon practice; best laid when the app's moon is new.
spreads.how: Deal in a crescent from the bottom up.

positions.label: Where I am
positions.meaning: What I bring into the new cycle.

positions.label: What to plant
positions.meaning: The intention that wants to grow.

positions.label: What feeds it
positions.meaning: What will help it grow.

positions.label: What to clear
positions.meaning: What would choke it.

positions.label: First step
positions.meaning: What to do before the moon is full.

spreads.read: Read again at the full moon with the full-moon spread.

spreads.name: Full moon
spreads.for: The full moon: harvest and release.
spreads.tradition: Modern moon practice; pairs with the new-moon spread.
spreads.how: Deal four around and one in the centre.

positions.label: What is lit
positions.meaning: What the full light shows.

positions.label: What has grown
positions.meaning: What came of the new moon's intention.

positions.label: What to celebrate
positions.meaning: The harvest.

positions.label: What to release
positions.meaning: What to let go as the moon wanes.

positions.label: What comes next
positions.meaning: The lesson carried into the dark.

spreads.read: Compare with your new-moon cards. Did the planted card's suit or number appear again?

spreads.name: The shadow
spreads.for: Facing what you hide from yourself. Slow and gentle; one at a time.
spreads.tradition: Modern, built on the old teaching that the devil you face becomes an ally.
spreads.how: Deal 1 face up; turn the others one at a time, waiting between each.

positions.label: The mask
positions.meaning: What I show the world.

positions.label: The shadow
positions.meaning: What I keep out of sight.

positions.label: Its root
positions.meaning: Where it came from.

positions.label: Its gift
positions.meaning: What it has been protecting, the strength inside it.

positions.label: The way home
positions.meaning: How to bring it back into the light.

spreads.read: End with something kind and ordinary: tea, a walk, a name for the day.

spreads.name: The line of five
spreads.for: Reading cards as a sentence, the Marseille way, with no fixed positions.
spreads.tradition: French cartomancy; works best with the Marseille deck, whose pips have no scenes.
spreads.how: Deal five cards in a row. No positions: the middle card is the subject, the cards either side are what acts on it.

positions.label: Left
positions.meaning: Read with the others.

positions.label: Left of centre
positions.meaning: Read with the others.

positions.label: The heart
positions.meaning: The subject of the sentence.

positions.label: Right of centre
positions.meaning: Read with the others.

positions.label: Right
positions.meaning: Read with the others.

spreads.read: Follow the gaze: a figure looking left looks at the past or at the card on its left, looking right looks ahead. A figure turning its back on a card refuses or leaves it. Read pairs mirrored around the centre (1 with 5, 2 with 4) and let the centre card answer them. Pips speak by number and by the shape of their pattern (crowded, open, crossed, flowering).

majority.major: strong forces beyond the asker's control
majority.Ace: strength generally; Aces are always strong cards

wands.name: Wands
wands.domain: will, drive, desire, creativity, ambition, spirit in motion

swords.name: Swords
swords.domain: mind, words, truth, conflict, decisions, pain that teaches

pentacles.name: Pentacles
pentacles.domain: body, money, work, home, craft, the real world

1.theme: the seed: the whole force of the suit before it takes any shape

2.theme: the first polarity: a choice, a meeting, a balance being found

3.theme: the first form: growth, creation, something born from two

4.theme: structure and rest: stability that can turn into stagnation

5.theme: disruption: conflict, loss or challenge that breaks the rut

6.theme: harmony restored: the heart of the suit, success, generosity

7.theme: testing: courage, imagination, effort that has not yet paid

8.theme: movement and method: skill, speed, patterns, the mind at work

9.theme: the near-peak: the suit at full intensity, for better or worse

10.theme: the end of the cycle: the suit fully made real, completion or overload

symbols: cliff edge = the unknown and the leap
white rose = innocence and pure desire
bundle = everything carried from before, kept light
white dog = instinct, loyalty, the warning bark
white sun = spirit watching over the start
snowy peaks = the heights still ahead
cards.upright: A new journey that starts before you feel ready. The Fool is pure potential: the zero before any number, the breath before the first word. Trust, curiosity and a light heart carry you further now than a plan would.
cards.reversed: Either the leap is reckless or you are frozen at the edge. Look at which: carelessness that ignores a real cliff, or fear that keeps you from a step you already know is yours. Sometimes the card asks you to wait one more day and pack properly.
cards.love: A fresh, unguarded start; falling for someone or something new without a script.
cards.work: A new path, a risky idea, a job or venture outside your experience; beginner's luck is real here.
cards.spirit: The soul setting out; the first step of the great journey through the twenty-one doors.
cards.advice: Step forward with open hands, and look once at your feet.
cards.shadow: Running from responsibility and calling it freedom.
cards.picture: A young traveller in bright clothes walks toward a cliff edge under a white sun, a white rose in one hand and a small bundle on a staff over the shoulder, a white dog leaping at the heels, snowy peaks behind.
cards.question: What would I begin if I didn't need to know how it ends?
cards.cat: You're walking off a cliff holding a flower. I've seen worse plans. Not many.
cards.name: The Fool

names.golden_dawn: The Spirit of Aether

symbols: raised wand and pointing hand = as above, so below
infinity sign = endless power, the eternal loop
four tools on the table = the four elements, all at command
roses and lilies = desire and purity
serpent belt = eternity biting its own tail
cards.upright: Every tool you need is on the table in front of you. The Magician joins heaven and earth through focused will: an idea becomes real when attention, skill and action point the same way. This is the moment to begin, with intention.
cards.reversed: Power with nowhere honest to go. It can mean talent left unused, plans that never leave your head, or someone (perhaps you) using charm and sleight of hand to steer others. Check what is being performed and what is real.
cards.love: Charisma and initiative; making the first move; watch for a smooth talker.
cards.work: Skill meets opportunity: pitching, launching, building, selling. The right moment to act.
cards.spirit: The adept who draws force from above into form below; ritual, intention and will.
cards.advice: Choose one aim and put all four tools to it.
cards.shadow: Cleverness used to fool people, including yourself.
cards.picture: A figure in a white robe and red cloak raises a wand to the sky and points the other hand to the ground; an infinity sign floats above the head, and on the table lie a cup, a sword, a pentacle and a wand among roses and lilies.
cards.question: Which of my tools am I ignoring?
cards.cat: Every tool on the table and you're still asking me. Impressive, honestly.
cards.name: The Magician

names.golden_dawn: The Magus of Power

symbols: two pillars = the gate between opposites, severity and mercy
veil of pomegranates = the hidden world, the fertility of the unseen
crescent moon = intuition, cycles, the deep mind
half-hidden scroll = law that is only partly revealed
equal-armed cross = the elements in balance
cards.upright: The answer is already in you, under the noise. The High Priestess guards the veil between what is known and what is felt; she does not explain, she shows. Be still, watch your dreams, and trust the knowing that arrives without reasons.
cards.reversed: The inner voice is being talked over, by other people or by your own need to have everything spelled out. Secrets may be festering, or you may be cut off from your own depths. Go quiet before you decide anything.
cards.love: An attraction with depth and mystery; something unspoken; feelings not yet revealed.
cards.work: Hold your cards close: research, quiet observation, trusting your read of people.
cards.spirit: Initiation into the mysteries; the moon, the veil, the scroll of hidden law; psychic opening.
cards.advice: Listen more than you speak, and let your dreams have a vote.
cards.shadow: Coldness and secrecy used as a wall.
cards.picture: A seated priestess in blue between a black pillar marked B and a white pillar marked J, a scroll marked TORA half hidden in her lap, a crescent moon at her feet, a veil of pomegranates behind her.
cards.question: What do I already know that I haven't admitted?
cards.cat: You already know. You just want someone else to say it so it's their fault.
cards.name: The High Priestess

names.golden_dawn: The Priestess of the Silver Star

symbols: ripe wheat = harvest and fertility
heart shield with Venus = love and beauty
twelve-star crown = the year, the zodiac, rule over nature's cycles
waterfall = feeling flowing into life
pomegranate gown = abundance
cards.upright: Life growing as it is meant to. The Empress is the abundant mother of the world: fertile ground, comfort, pleasure, art and the body enjoyed. What you planted is coming up; feed it, rest in it, let yourself receive.
cards.reversed: The garden is overgrown or bare. Care can turn into smothering, comfort into inertia, or you may be giving to everyone except yourself. If creative energy feels blocked, go back to the senses, to nature, to making something with your hands.
cards.love: Warmth, devotion, sensual pleasure; a nurturing bond; a home being made together.
cards.work: Creative projects flourish; growth through patience; beauty, design, hospitality, care.
cards.spirit: The great mother, Venus on earth; the door through which spirit enters form.
cards.advice: Nourish what you've started, and let yourself be nourished too.
cards.shadow: Love that holds on too tightly for anything to grow up.
cards.picture: A woman crowned with twelve stars sits on cushions in a field of ripe wheat, a heart-shaped shield marked with the sign of Venus beside her, a forest and a waterfall behind.
cards.question: What in my life wants more care, and what wants less?
cards.cat: You're blooming. Try not to water the weeds this time.
cards.name: The Empress

names.golden_dawn: The Daughter of the Mighty Ones

symbols: ram heads = Aries, initiative, drive
ankh sceptre = power over life
orb = rule over the world
armour under the robe = always ready to defend
bare mountains = hard-won ground, discipline over comfort
cards.upright: Order, boundaries and the will to build. The Emperor brings law to chaos: plans, rules, responsibility and the strength to protect what matters. Take charge, set the structure, and lead from experience rather than mood.
cards.reversed: Structure gone wrong in one of two directions: control that has become tyranny and stubbornness, or no backbone, plan or boundary at all. Look at who holds power here, and whether it is earned.
cards.love: Commitment, reliability and protection; or a partner who needs to control.
cards.work: Leadership, management, a boss or an institution; building the framework; contracts and order.
cards.spirit: The ram's fire of Aries; the sovereign self who rules an inner kingdom.
cards.advice: Build the structure first, then let it hold you, not cage you.
cards.shadow: Mistaking control for safety.
cards.picture: A bearded ruler in armour under red robes sits on a stone throne carved with ram heads, an ankh sceptre in one hand and an orb in the other, bare red mountains behind him.
cards.question: Where do I need firmer boundaries, and where am I gripping too hard?
cards.cat: You want to be in charge. Start with the laundry pile, your majesty.
cards.name: The Emperor

names.golden_dawn: Son of the Morning, Chief among the Mighty

cards.thoth_note: The Thoth deck gives the Emperor the letter Tzaddi and the Star the letter Heh (the signs stay: Aries, Aquarius), so they swap paths 15 and 28.

symbols: crossed keys = the keys to the outer and inner mysteries
triple crown and cross = rule over three worlds
two followers = the teaching passed on
hand raised in blessing = what is above, given to those below
pillars = the temple and its law
cards.upright: The wisdom handed down. The Hierophant is the teacher, the lineage, the rite that has worked for centuries. Seek a mentor, learn the system before you break it, and find strength in people who share your values.
cards.reversed: Tradition has become a cage, or you are being called off the path everyone expects. It can also point to empty ritual, hypocrisy in an institution, or obedience without understanding. Question the rule, then decide.
cards.love: Commitment in the eyes of the world; shared values; a traditional union.
cards.work: Established institutions, education, credentials, following procedure, a mentor.
cards.spirit: Initiation within a lineage; the keys of the mysteries; the bridge between heaven and the people.
cards.advice: Learn from those who walked here first, then make the teaching your own.
cards.shadow: Handing your conscience to an authority.
cards.picture: A robed and crowned religious figure sits between two grey pillars, raising a hand in blessing and holding a triple cross; two followers kneel before him and two crossed keys lie at his feet.
cards.question: Whose rules am I following, and do I still believe them?
cards.cat: You want a guru. You'd be arguing with one inside a week.
cards.name: The Hierophant

names.golden_dawn: The Magus of the Eternal

symbols: angel = blessing from above, the higher self
tree with serpent = desire, temptation, knowledge
tree of flames = passion and spirit
mountain = the summit reached together
nakedness = honesty, nothing hidden
cards.upright: A union and a choice. The Lovers is love in its deepest sense, two becoming whole without losing themselves, under a blessing from above. It is also a crossroads where you choose by your truest values, because what you choose here, you become.
cards.reversed: Something is out of alignment: between partners, or between what you want and what you believe. It can show temptation, a bond pulling you away from yourself, or a decision avoided until it decides for you.
cards.love: Deep attraction, a meaningful partnership, a love that asks something of you.
cards.work: A partnership or a values-based decision; choose the path you can stand behind.
cards.spirit: The sacred marriage of opposites within; Gemini, the twins, the waking mind and the deep mind meeting.
cards.advice: Choose with your whole heart, and stand behind it.
cards.shadow: Choosing what is easy to want over what is right to want.
cards.picture: A naked man and woman stand in a garden under a great winged angel and a blazing sun; behind the woman a tree with a serpent and fruit, behind the man a tree of flames, a mountain between them.
cards.question: What am I really choosing when I choose this?
cards.cat: Big choice. You'll pick with your pulse, then ask me to bless it.
cards.name: The Lovers

names.golden_dawn: The Children of the Voice; the Oracle of the Mighty Gods

symbols: black and white sphinxes = opposing forces under one will
no reins = control by will alone
starry canopy = protection from heaven
crescent moons on the shoulders = Cancer and the moon, feeling in armour
city behind = what is left behind on the way to victory
cards.upright: Victory through will. The Chariot holds opposing forces in check and drives them toward one goal. Focus, discipline and confidence win this one; keep your hands steady and your eyes on the road.
cards.reversed: The horses are pulling in different directions. Force without direction, aggression without aim, or a goal you no longer believe in. Stop, take back the reins, and decide where you are actually going.
cards.love: Pursuing what you want with confidence; a relationship moving forward; or a battle of wills.
cards.work: Ambition, competition and a win; the push to the finish; travel for work.
cards.spirit: The self as charioteer of the soul; mastery of the inner animals; the armoured shell of Cancer.
cards.advice: Hold the reins, pick the destination, then go.
cards.shadow: Winning at any cost and calling it strength.
cards.picture: An armoured prince stands in a stone chariot under a canopy of stars, a walled city behind; two sphinxes, one black and one white, lie before it with no reins, held only by his will.
cards.question: What am I steering toward, and what is steering me?
cards.cat: Full speed, no map. Classic you. At least you look good doing it.
cards.name: The Chariot

names.golden_dawn: The Child of the Powers of the Waters; the Lord of the Triumph of Light

symbols: lion = passion, instinct, raw force
gentle hands = mastery through love, not violence
infinity sign = inner power that never runs out
flower crown and belt = nature tamed with grace
white robe = purity of intent
cards.upright: Strength that doesn't need to shout. A gentle hand closes the lion's jaws: courage, patience and compassion master the wild forces, inside and out. Trust your inner power and meet fierceness with calm.
cards.reversed: The lion is winning, or the hand has turned to force. Self-doubt, anger, burnout, or trying to dominate what only patience can tame. Find your footing again with kindness to yourself first.
cards.love: Tenderness and passion together; patience with a partner; a bond that tames old wounds.
cards.work: Steady confidence, leadership through influence, perseverance under pressure.
cards.spirit: The serpent fire of Teth and Leo; desire harnessed, never killed; the beast and the woman in union.
cards.advice: Be gentle and fearless at once.
cards.shadow: Pretending to be calm while the lion eats you from inside.
cards.picture: A woman in white, crowned with flowers, an infinity sign above her head, calmly closes the jaws of a red lion with her hands, in an open landscape under a yellow sky.
cards.question: What wild thing in me needs a gentle hand instead of a cage?
cards.cat: You're stronger than you act. Annoying that it takes a lion to prove it.
cards.name: Strength

names.golden_dawn: The Daughter of the Flaming Sword; the Leader of the Lion

numbering.note: Strength is VIII and Justice XI in the 1909 London deck; the older order (and the Thoth deck) has Justice VIII and Strength XI

symbols: lantern with six-pointed star = the light of wisdom, as above so below
grey cloak = silence, going unseen
snowy peak = attainment, isolation, height
staff = the support of experience
night = the inner journey
cards.upright: The light you need is the one you carry. The Hermit leaves the noise to climb a mountain of his own, lantern raised, and finds truth in silence. Take time alone, study, reflect; or seek out the one teacher who walked this path before you.
cards.reversed: Solitude has turned into isolation, or you are dodging the inner work by staying busy and loud. It can also mean the retreat is over: time to come down the mountain and share what you found.
cards.love: Time alone to understand yourself; a slow, thoughtful bond; space needed.
cards.work: Research, specialist knowledge, mentoring, working alone; a pause to rethink direction.
cards.spirit: The seeker with the star in the lamp; the virgin wisdom of Virgo; initiation by silence.
cards.advice: Go quiet, go inward, and follow your own light.
cards.shadow: Calling loneliness wisdom so you never have to risk anyone.
cards.picture: An old man in a grey cloak stands on a snowy peak at night, holding up a lantern with a six-pointed star inside and leaning on a long staff.
cards.question: What can I only hear when I'm alone?
cards.cat: Off to find yourself again. Take snacks. You get grumpy.
cards.name: The Hermit

names.golden_dawn: The Magus of the Voice of Power; the Prophet of the Eternal

symbols: wheel with letters and the divine name = the law of cycles
sphinx = wisdom above the turning
serpent descending = the fall
jackal-headed figure rising = the climb back up
four winged creatures = the fixed signs, the steady world around change
cards.upright: The wheel turns. Fortune rises and falls in cycles larger than any one person, and right now it is moving. A turning point, a lucky break, a destined meeting: go with the current and act when the moment comes round.
cards.reversed: The wheel feels stuck or turning down: delays, setbacks, a pattern you keep repeating. Resistance makes it worse. Ask what you keep doing that brings you back to the same place, and change that.
cards.love: A fated meeting or a change in a relationship's cycle; what goes around comes around.
cards.work: Opportunity, unexpected developments, a change of fortune; timing matters more than effort.
cards.spirit: Jupiter's wheel; the turning of karma; the still hub at the centre where the wise one sits.
cards.advice: Ride the turn; the moment is now.
cards.shadow: Blaming fate for what is your choice.
cards.picture: A great wheel marked with letters and alchemical signs turns in the clouds; a sphinx with a sword sits on top, a serpent slides down one side and a jackal-headed figure rises on the other, and four winged creatures read books in the corners.
cards.question: What cycle am I in, and where on the wheel am I standing?
cards.cat: Luck's turning. Don't do anything stupid with it. I'm looking at you.
cards.name: Wheel of Fortune

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of the Forces of Life

symbols: upright sword = discernment, the cut of truth
scales = balance, cause and effect
crown = the authority of law
pillars and veil = the hall of judgement, truth behind appearances
one foot forward = justice that acts
cards.upright: Truth weighed and consequences delivered. Justice sees cause and effect clearly: what you put in, you get back. Be honest, take responsibility, make the fair decision; legal and official matters favour whoever is in the right.
cards.reversed: The scales are off. Something unfair, a lie, a refusal to own your part, or a judgement clouded by bias. The truth is still there to be faced, and the longer it waits the heavier it gets.
cards.love: Fairness and balance between partners; honest talk; a bond judged by how both give.
cards.work: Contracts, legal matters, decisions, integrity; you get what you have earned.
cards.spirit: Karma made visible; the sword of discernment; Libra's balance and the adjustment of all things.
cards.advice: Tell the truth and let it cut cleanly.
cards.shadow: Judging others by a law you excuse yourself from.
cards.picture: A crowned figure in red sits between two pillars, an upright double-edged sword in the right hand and golden scales in the left, a purple veil behind.
cards.question: What is the honest truth here, including my part in it?
cards.cat: A fair outcome is coming. Hope you were fair. Were you? Thought so.
cards.name: Justice

names.golden_dawn: The Daughter of the Lords of Truth; the Ruler of the Balance

numbering.note: Strength is VIII and Justice XI in the 1909 London deck; the older order (and the Thoth deck) has Justice VIII and Strength XI

symbols: hanging by one foot = surrender chosen freely
halo = insight born of the reversal
living tree = the tree of life, the cross of growth
crossed leg = the figure four, the cross of the elements
calm face = peace inside the pause
cards.upright: Everything stops so you can see it upside down. The Hanged Man surrenders by choice, hangs calm and haloed, and gains a vision no struggle could give. Pause, let go of control, give up something small for something true.
cards.reversed: Suspension without insight: stalling, playing the martyr, or sacrificing for nothing. Or the opposite: the long wait is ending and you are finally coming down. Ask what you are refusing to release.
cards.love: A relationship on hold; seeing a partner differently; giving without resentment, or not.
cards.work: Delays, a project paused; rethink before acting; an unconventional approach pays off.
cards.spirit: The suspended initiate; the baptism of Mem's water; the god who hangs on the tree to win wisdom.
cards.advice: Stop fighting, and turn the question upside down.
cards.shadow: Waiting forever and calling it patience.
cards.picture: A man hangs upside down by one foot from a living T-shaped tree, the other leg bent behind the knee, hands behind his back, his face calm and a halo of light around his head.
cards.question: What would change if I stopped struggling and looked from the other side?
cards.cat: Hanging around again. Very spiritual. Also exactly what you did last month.
cards.name: The Hanged Man

names.golden_dawn: The Spirit of the Mighty Waters

symbols: armoured skeleton = what lies under every life, untouched by change
white rose banner = purity and rebirth beyond the end
fallen king = no rank escapes change
sun rising between towers = the new day after
river and boat = passage to the other shore
cards.upright: An ending that makes room. Death is transformation: a chapter closes, a skin is shed, and what was cannot come back. It speaks of change, not of bodies: the great door every new life passes through. Let it go cleanly.
cards.reversed: Something should have ended and hasn't. Clinging to a situation that is already over, dreading change, or a transition dragging on. The release will come either way; letting go on purpose makes it kinder.
cards.love: A relationship transforms or ends; an old pattern finishes; love reborn on new terms.
cards.work: A job, role or project ends; restructuring; one path closes and another opens.
cards.spirit: Scorpio's alchemy; the lord of the gates; the old self dissolving so the new one can rise.
cards.advice: Let the ending finish so the beginning can start.
cards.shadow: Refusing every ending and rotting in place.
cards.picture: A skeleton in black armour rides a white horse, carrying a black banner with a white rose; a king lies fallen, a bishop pleads, a child and a maiden wait, and a sun rises between two towers on the horizon.
cards.question: What am I ready to let end?
cards.cat: Something's over. You knew. You just liked the drama of not knowing.
cards.name: Death

names.golden_dawn: The Child of the Great Transformers; the Lord of the Gates of Death

symbols: water poured between cups = the flow between the waking and the deep mind, alchemy
one foot in water, one on land = balance between feeling and the material
triangle in a square on the chest = spirit within matter
path to the crown = the long road to attainment
irises = the rainbow messenger, hope
cards.upright: The art of mixing the right things in the right measure. Temperance pours between two cups without spilling: patience, moderation and the slow alchemy that turns opposites into something new. Things mend and come together in their own time.
cards.reversed: The mixture is off. Excess, rushing, extremes, or two parts of your life that refuse to blend. Find the middle again: slow down, and take one thing out of the cup.
cards.love: Harmony, compromise, a calm and healing bond; two different people blending well.
cards.work: Cooperation, steady progress, good management, the right balance of effort.
cards.spirit: The art of the alchemist; the arrow of Sagittarius; the angel who reconciles fire and water.
cards.advice: Be patient; blend, don't force.
cards.shadow: Lukewarm everything; never committing to any flame.
cards.picture: A winged angel with one foot on land and one in a pool pours water between two golden cups; a path runs from the pool to a crown of light over distant mountains, and irises bloom at the side.
cards.question: What in my life needs a little less, and what needs a little more?
cards.cat: Moderation, says the card. Not you, clearly.
cards.name: Temperance

names.golden_dawn: The Daughter of the Reconcilers; the Bringer-Forth of Life

symbols: loose chains = bonds that could be taken off
inverted pentagram = spirit under matter
lowered torch = fire turned toward the earth, desire
horns and tails on the couple = becoming what they serve
black pedestal = the half-cube of the material world
cards.upright: The chains are loose enough to lift off, but you have to notice them first. The Devil shows what binds you: a habit, a craving, a fear, a bond that feeds on you, the lure of money or power. It is also raw life force and desire; the question is whether you own it or it owns you.
cards.reversed: The chains begin to come off: seeing a pattern for what it is, walking away from a bond, reclaiming your power. Or a warning of slipping back. Either way, the shadow is in the light now and can be worked with.
cards.love: Intense attraction, obsession, possessiveness, or a bond held together by something other than love.
cards.work: Golden handcuffs, a job you stay in for the money, power games, ambition turning greedy.
cards.spirit: The gate of matter; Capricorn's goat; the shadow you must face and take back to rise.
cards.advice: Name the chain, then lift it off your neck.
cards.shadow: Saying you have no choice when you do.
cards.picture: A horned, bat-winged devil crouches on a black pedestal, a torch pointing down; a naked man and woman with small horns and tails stand chained to the pedestal by loose collars.
cards.question: What am I calling a need that is really a habit or a fear?
cards.cat: Those chains are loose. You just like the jewellery.
cards.name: The Devil

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of the Gates of Matter; the Child of the Forces of Time

symbols: lightning = sudden truth from above
crown blown off = pride and false certainty overthrown
falling figures = no one is spared the revelation
drops of fire = grace hidden inside the disaster
rocky peak = a high place built in isolation
cards.upright: Lightning strikes what was built on a false foundation. The Tower is sudden, shocking change: a revelation, a collapse, a truth that cannot be unseen. It is frightening and it is liberation. What falls now was never going to hold.
cards.reversed: The collapse is being held off, or it is happening inside rather than out. You may be bracing against a change that needs to come, or living through the aftershock. Let the false structure go before the storm makes the choice.
cards.love: A shock, a revelation, a break-up or a breakthrough; a relationship's false walls come down.
cards.work: Sudden change, restructuring, a plan that collapses; the clearing before a better build.
cards.spirit: The lightning flash of revelation; Mars and the mouth of Peh; the tower of the ego struck by heaven's fire.
cards.advice: Let it fall, then build on rock.
cards.shadow: Building again on the same cracked ground.
cards.picture: A tall tower on a rocky peak is struck by lightning; its crown is blown off, flames burst from the windows and two figures fall headfirst through the dark among drops of fire.
cards.question: What in my life is built on something I already know is false?
cards.cat: Kaboom. You built it on sand and fibs. Even I saw that, and I nap all day.
cards.name: The Tower

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of the Hosts of the Mighty

symbols: great star = guidance, the higher self
seven small stars = the planets, the lights of the soul
water onto land and into the pool = feeding the waking and the deep mind
nakedness = vulnerability, truth
ibis = the bird of wisdom and the soul
cards.upright: After the storm, the sky clears. The Star is hope and renewal: quiet faith, healing, a sense of being guided. Pour yourself out freely and trust that the source refills. Dreams and long-held wishes are blessed now.
cards.reversed: The light seems far away: discouragement, loss of faith in yourself or the future, giving freely with nothing coming back. The star hasn't gone anywhere. Look up again, and let yourself be helped.
cards.love: Healing love, honest openness, a gentle new start; feeling seen.
cards.work: Inspiration, a calling, recognition arriving slowly; creative and visionary work.
cards.spirit: The daughter of the firmament; Aquarius pouring the waters of life; the guiding star of the soul.
cards.advice: Have faith, and pour.
cards.shadow: Hoping instead of acting.
cards.picture: A naked woman kneels by a pool under one great eight-pointed star and seven smaller ones, pouring water from one jug into the pool and from another onto the land; an ibis sits in a tree behind her.
cards.question: What would I do if I trusted that I am being guided?
cards.cat: Hope. Cute. Now go and do something about it.
cards.name: The Star

names.golden_dawn: The Daughter of the Firmament; the Dweller between the Waters

cards.thoth_note: The Thoth deck gives the Star the letter Heh and the Emperor Tzaddi (the signs stay), so they swap paths 28 and 15.

symbols: moon with a face = reflected light, the dreaming mind
dog and wolf = the tame and the wild instinct
crayfish from the pool = what rises from the depths
two towers = the gate into the unknown
winding path = the way through uncertainty
cards.upright: The path is lit, but only by moonlight. The Moon brings dreams, instinct, fear and illusion; things are not as they seem, and the deep mind is speaking. Walk carefully, trust your instinct over your fear, and don't sign anything in the dark.
cards.reversed: The fog begins to lift, or what was hidden comes up to the surface. Fears are named, deceptions exposed, intuition clears. It can also show anxiety kept underground; let it out into the light.
cards.love: Uncertainty, secrets, projection, romantic illusion; or a deep, psychic bond.
cards.work: Unclear information, hidden factors, creative and intuitive work; wait for clarity.
cards.spirit: The dreaming path between the towers; Pisces and the back of the head; the psychic tides.
cards.advice: Trust your instinct, check your facts, wait for daylight.
cards.shadow: Believing every fear the dark tells you.
cards.picture: A full moon with a face drips dew between two towers; a dog and a wolf howl at it, a crayfish crawls up out of a pool, and a narrow path winds away toward distant mountains.
cards.question: What am I afraid of, and is it real?
cards.cat: Spooked by shadows again. Some are real. Most are your coat on a chair.
cards.name: The Moon

names.golden_dawn: The Ruler of Flux and Reflux; the Child of the Sons of the Mighty

symbols: smiling sun = joy, awareness, life force
child = innocence regained, the new self
white horse = pure energy carrying you
sunflowers = growth turned toward the light
wall = the garden left behind, safety outgrown
cards.upright: Everything is lit. The Sun is joy, success, warmth and plain truth: things are good and can be seen for what they are. Confidence, play, achievement, being loved for exactly who you are. Enjoy it fully.
cards.reversed: The sun is behind a cloud, not gone. Joy is dimmed, success delayed, or confidence has turned into showing off. Look for the simple things that still make you glad.
cards.love: Happiness, warmth, a relationship full of light and play; love freely shown.
cards.work: Success, recognition, clarity, a project that shines; a great time to be seen.
cards.spirit: The lord of the fire of the world; the child of light; the soul's radiance after the night of the Moon.
cards.advice: Shine, play, and let yourself be seen.
cards.shadow: Needing to be the centre of every room.
cards.picture: A naked child crowned with flowers rides a white horse with arms flung wide, holding a red banner, under a huge smiling sun; tall sunflowers grow over a wall behind.
cards.question: What makes me glad to be alive, and when did I last do it?
cards.cat: Fine, you're glowing. Stop squinting at it like it's a trick.
cards.name: The Sun

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of the Fire of the World

symbols: trumpet = the call that wakes the soul
rising figures = rebirth of every part of the self
open coffins on water = what was buried, carried up by feeling
banner with a cross = the elements in balance, a new order
mountains = the heights of the awakened life
cards.upright: The trumpet sounds and you rise. Judgement is awakening: a calling you can't ignore, a reckoning with the past that frees you from it, a rebirth into a larger life. Answer the call; forgive, and be forgiven.
cards.reversed: The call is ringing and you are pretending not to hear it, or judging yourself so harshly you can't get up. Old regret is keeping you in the ground. Lay the past down and stand.
cards.love: A relationship reborn, a second chance, a reckoning between partners; a decision about the future.
cards.work: A calling, a big decision, the moment to step up; past effort finally judged and rewarded.
cards.spirit: The primal fire of Shin; the angel's trumpet; the rising of the true self in a new age.
cards.advice: Listen for your name, and rise.
cards.shadow: Being your own merciless judge.
cards.picture: A great angel in the clouds blows a trumpet hung with a cross-marked banner; below, grey men, women and children rise from open coffins floating on water, arms raised, with mountains behind.
cards.question: What is calling me, and what is keeping me from answering?
cards.cat: Someone's calling your name. It isn't me. I don't call. Go.
cards.name: Judgement

names.golden_dawn: The Spirit of the Primal Fire

symbols: wreath = the cycle completed, the cosmic egg
dancer = the soul in perfect motion
two wands = power held in balance
four creatures = the four fixed signs and elements in harmony
ribbons tied like infinity = endless renewal
cards.upright: The circle closes. The World is completion and wholeness: a cycle finished, a goal reached, every part of you dancing in one body. Celebrate, gather the lessons, and know that a new journey begins at the end of this one.
cards.reversed: Not quite finished. A loose end, a missing piece, an ending you keep postponing, or a shortcut that left the circle open. Finish what you started, then you can go.
cards.love: Fulfilment, a complete partnership, a sense of having arrived; love across distance going well.
cards.work: Success, completion of a major project, international work, recognition.
cards.spirit: The great one of the night of time; Saturn and the earth; the soul dancing at the centre of creation, the end of the Fool's journey.
cards.advice: Finish it, celebrate it, and take the next step.
cards.shadow: Refusing to finish anything so you never have to start again.
cards.picture: A dancing figure wrapped in a violet sash holds a wand in each hand inside a great oval wreath tied with red ribbons; in the four corners a man, an eagle, a lion and a bull look on from the clouds.
cards.question: What am I ready to complete, and what has it taught me?
cards.cat: You finished something. Mark the calendar. It's rarer than an eclipse.
cards.name: The World

names.golden_dawn: The Great One of the Night of Time

cards.upright: The first flame. A burst of inspiration, a new passion, a project or desire that wants to be born now. The Ace of Wands is pure creative fire: grab it while it burns and turn it into the first action.
cards.reversed: The spark is there but won't catch. Delays, low energy, plans that keep slipping, or excitement spent on talk instead of doing. Shelter the flame and feed it something small and real.
cards.love: Sudden attraction, a passionate start, a rekindled flame.
cards.work: A new project, idea or business; a creative opportunity; the go-ahead.
cards.spirit: The root of the powers of fire; the will of spirit seeking a body.
cards.advice: Act on the spark today, before it cools.
cards.picture: A hand reaches out of a cloud holding a stout budding wand, leaves falling from it, over green hills, a river and a distant castle.
cards.question: What wants to be started through me?
cards.cat: Ooh, a spark. You'll either light a fire or set your eyebrows on it.
cards.name: Ace of Wands

names.golden_dawn: The Root of the Powers of Fire

cards.number_meaning: the seed: the whole force of the suit before it takes any shape
cards.rules: A quadrant of the heavens around the North Pole, over Cancer, Leo, Virgo (shared with the Princess of the suit)

cards.upright: You have the world in your hand and must decide what to do with it. The Two of Wands is the moment after the spark: making plans, looking beyond familiar walls, choosing a direction. Dominion is yours if you leave the battlements.
cards.reversed: Restless inside safe walls. Fear of the unknown, a plan that never leaves the drawing board, or choosing comfort over the bigger life you can see from the roof.
cards.love: Deciding whether to commit or move on; long-distance plans; choosing between the familiar and the new.
cards.work: Strategy, expansion plans, partnerships, choosing a market or a path.
cards.spirit: The lord of dominion; Mars in Aries; will finding its first direction.
cards.advice: Make the plan, then step outside the walls.
cards.picture: A man in a red hat stands on a castle roof holding a small globe, one wand in his hand and another fixed to the wall, gazing over sea and land; a cross of roses and lilies is set into the stone.
cards.question: What would I attempt if I really owned my power?
cards.cat: You're holding the planet like a snow globe. Put it down and go somewhere.
cards.name: Two of Wands

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Dominion

cards.number_meaning: the first polarity: a choice, a meeting, a balance being found

cards.upright: The ships are on the water. The Three of Wands is plans in motion: early results, expansion, looking ahead with confidence. Keep your vision wide; what you sent out is on its way back.
cards.reversed: The ships are late. Delays, setbacks in growth, plans that were too small or too rushed. It can also show refusing to look past the immediate. Adjust the route rather than abandoning the voyage.
cards.love: A relationship growing; long-distance love; looking to the future together.
cards.work: Growth, export, travel, a business expanding; early success from earlier effort.
cards.spirit: The lord of established strength; the Sun in Aries; vision held steady.
cards.advice: Look further out; your reach is longer than you think.
cards.picture: A figure in a cloak stands on a clifftop with back turned, one hand on one of three planted wands, watching ships sail across a golden sea.
cards.question: What have I already set in motion that I need to trust?
cards.cat: Waiting for your ship to come in. It's coming. Your patience isn't.
cards.name: Three of Wands

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Established Strength

cards.number_meaning: the first form: growth, creation, something born from two

cards.upright: A celebration under the garland. The Four of Wands is a homecoming, a milestone, a wedding, a party: work completed and enjoyed with the people you love. Stability that feels like freedom.
cards.reversed: The celebration is postponed or shaky. Tension at home, a move or transition, feeling unwelcome, or joy held back until everything is perfect. Celebrate the small win now.
cards.love: Engagement, marriage, moving in together, a joyful stage of the relationship.
cards.work: A completed project, a launch party, a happy team, a good place to work.
cards.spirit: The lord of perfected work; Venus in Aries; the four pillars of a temple raised.
cards.advice: Gather your people and celebrate what you built.
cards.picture: Four wands are planted in the ground with a garland of flowers and fruit hung between them; two figures raise bouquets in welcome, and a castle stands behind.
cards.question: What deserves celebrating that I keep rushing past?
cards.cat: A party. For you. I'll attend for the food and leave early.
cards.name: Four of Wands

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Perfected Work

cards.number_meaning: structure and rest: stability that can turn into stagnation

cards.upright: Everyone is swinging a stick and nobody is hitting anyone. The Five of Wands is competition, friction, a scrum of egos and ideas. It can be healthy sparring that sharpens you, or noise that goes nowhere. Pick what you are fighting for.
cards.reversed: The fighting stops, or goes underground. Conflict avoided for the sake of peace, an argument finally settled, or a war happening only in your own head. Find the common goal.
cards.love: Arguments, rivalry, playful or not-so-playful friction; competing priorities.
cards.work: Competition, office politics, brainstorming chaos, a crowded market.
cards.spirit: The lord of strife; Saturn in Leo; the forge where wills are tested.
cards.advice: Compete honestly, or step out of the scrum.
cards.picture: Five young men brandish wands at one another in a jumble that looks half like a game and half like a brawl.
cards.question: What am I actually fighting about?
cards.cat: Five people waving sticks. Very productive. You're the loud one, aren't you.
cards.name: Five of Wands

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Strife

cards.number_meaning: disruption: conflict, loss or challenge that breaks the rut

cards.upright: The victory ride. The Six of Wands is success that is seen: praise, promotion, a win, a public moment of pride. Enjoy the laurels; you earned them.
cards.reversed: The parade didn't come, or the crowd turned. Recognition withheld, ego swelling, success that feels hollow, or fear of being seen. Your worth doesn't depend on the applause.
cards.love: Feeling proud of each other; a relationship admired by others; winning someone's heart.
cards.work: Promotion, awards, a successful launch, good reviews.
cards.spirit: The lord of victory; Jupiter in Leo; confidence as a spiritual force.
cards.advice: Accept the win graciously, and remember who carried the wands with you.
cards.picture: A rider crowned with laurel on a white horse carries a wand topped by a laurel wreath, followed by people on foot carrying wands.
cards.question: Can I let myself be celebrated?
cards.cat: Victory lap. Wave. Don't trip off the horse in front of everyone.
cards.name: Six of Wands

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Victory

cards.number_meaning: harmony restored: the heart of the suit, success, generosity

cards.upright: Holding the high ground against many. The Seven of Wands is standing up for what you believe while others push back. You have the advantage of position; keep your footing and defend it.
cards.reversed: Worn down by the fight. Overwhelm, the urge to give up, or defending things that don't need defending. Choose which battles are worth your energy.
cards.love: Defending a relationship, setting boundaries, standing up to outside pressure.
cards.work: Competitive pressure, defending your position, holding a line in negotiation.
cards.spirit: The lord of valour; Mars in Leo; courage when outnumbered.
cards.advice: Hold your ground; it's yours.
cards.picture: A young man on a rise defends himself with one wand against six wands thrust up at him from below; he wears mismatched shoes, as if he dressed in a hurry.
cards.question: What am I willing to stand up for, and what can I let go?
cards.cat: You against everyone again. Odd shoes, though. Very brave.
cards.name: Seven of Wands

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Valour

cards.number_meaning: testing: courage, imagination, effort that has not yet paid

cards.upright: Everything moves at once. The Eight of Wands is speed and momentum: messages, travel, fast developments, things finally landing. Act quickly and stay on top of it.
cards.reversed: The arrows are stuck in the air. Delays, crossed messages, rushing into mistakes, or energy scattered in too many directions. Slow down to aim.
cards.love: Swift romance, messages flying, a sudden development; or mixed signals.
cards.work: Rapid progress, deadlines, news arriving, a fast-moving project.
cards.spirit: The lord of swiftness; Mercury in Sagittarius; the arrows of thought released.
cards.advice: Move with the momentum while it lasts.
cards.picture: Eight wands fly through a clear sky in parallel, sloping down over open country and a river toward the ground.
cards.question: What is speeding toward me that I need to be ready for?
cards.cat: Everything's happening at once. You'll check your phone forty times. I'll nap.
cards.name: Eight of Wands

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Swiftness

cards.number_meaning: movement and method: skill, speed, patterns, the mind at work

cards.upright: Battered, bandaged and still standing. The Nine of Wands is resilience at the end of a long fight: you have one more push in you. Guard what you've won, and know the finish is close.
cards.reversed: So tired you suspect everyone. Exhaustion, defensiveness, walls so high nobody can help you over them, or quitting one step from the end. Let someone stand guard for a while.
cards.love: Old hurts making you guarded; persistence through a hard patch.
cards.work: Endurance, a final push, defending your work against criticism.
cards.spirit: The lord of great strength; the Moon in Sagittarius; the strength that remains when strength is gone.
cards.advice: One more effort, then rest.
cards.picture: A man with a bandaged head leans on a wand and looks warily over his shoulder, eight more wands standing behind him like a fence.
cards.question: What am I guarding, and is it still under attack?
cards.cat: You look like you've fought a hedge and lost. You're nearly there. Keep the bandage.
cards.name: Nine of Wands

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Great Strength

cards.number_meaning: the near-peak: the suit at full intensity, for better or worse

cards.upright: Carrying everything, alone. The Ten of Wands is too much responsibility: success that turned into a burden, a load you keep picking up. The town is close, but you can't see it past the wands.
cards.reversed: The load is finally coming off, by choice or because you dropped it. Delegate, say no, put down what isn't yours. Or a warning: carrying on like this will break something.
cards.love: One partner carrying the relationship; duty crowding out joy.
cards.work: Overwork, heavy responsibilities, a project that grew too big.
cards.spirit: The lord of oppression; Saturn in Sagittarius; fire smothered by its own fuel.
cards.advice: Put some of it down. Not all of it is yours.
cards.picture: A man bends forward under the weight of ten wands clutched in his arms, struggling toward a house in the distance, his face hidden by the bundle.
cards.question: Which of these burdens did I pick up myself?
cards.cat: You're carrying ten sticks and refusing help. That's not strength. That's stubborn.
cards.name: Ten of Wands

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Oppression

cards.number_meaning: the end of the cycle: the suit fully made real, completion or overload

cards.upright: The eager messenger. The Page of Wands brings news, a spark of interest, a new passion to explore. It is the beginner's fire: curious, bold, full of ideas, not yet tested. Follow what excites you.
cards.reversed: All spark, no follow-through. False starts, scattered interests, impatience, or news you didn't want. Pick one flame and tend it.
cards.love: Flirtation, a playful new attraction, an exciting message.
cards.work: A new idea, an internship, an exploratory project, a creative beginning.
cards.spirit: The princess of the shining flame; earth of fire; spirit discovering what it loves.
cards.advice: Explore it like a beginner.
cards.person: A lively, adventurous young person or a beginner; restless, warm, full of ideas, easily bored.
cards.picture: A young person in a feathered hat and a tunic patterned with salamanders stands in a desert, holding a tall budding wand and gazing at its tip.
cards.question: What lights me up that I haven't let myself explore?
cards.cat: New obsession. Lovely. I give it three weeks. Prove me wrong.
cards.name: Page of Wands

names.golden_dawn: The Princess of the Shining Flame; the Rose of the Palace of Fire

court.rules: A quadrant of the heavens around the North Pole, over Cancer, Leo, Virgo

cards.upright: Charging in. The Knight of Wands is fire in motion: adventure, passion, a sudden move or journey, confidence that sweeps people along. Act boldly while the energy is hot.
cards.reversed: The horse bolts. Recklessness, impatience, anger, projects abandoned halfway, or charm that never stays. Channel the fire before it burns out.
cards.love: A passionate, exciting romance; or someone who rides off as fast as they arrived.
cards.work: Bold moves, travel, a change of job, a fast start; watch the follow-through.
cards.spirit: The lord of the flame and the lightning; fire of fire; the pure leap of will.
cards.advice: Go for it, and finish the ride.
cards.person: Daring, charming, impulsive, always on the move; thrilling company and hard to pin down.
cards.picture: A knight in armour, his tunic covered in salamanders, rears up on a horse in the desert, holding a budding wand, pyramids in the distance.
cards.question: Where am I rushing, and where should I charge?
cards.cat: Gallop, gallop. Where are you going? You don't know. Fabulous.
cards.name: Knight of Wands

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of the Flame and the Lightning; the King of the Spirits of Fire

cards.upright: The radiant one. The Queen of Wands is confident, warm, magnetic, fiercely herself. She makes things happen and draws people in. Own your light and lead with your heart.
cards.reversed: The fire turns hot and sharp. Jealousy, demands, insecurity, or a once-bright person running on empty. Refill yourself before you give more.
cards.love: Passionate, loyal, attractive; a confident partner.
cards.work: Leadership, visibility, creative direction, entrepreneurship.
cards.spirit: The queen of the thrones of flame; water of fire; the fire that warms rather than consumes.
cards.advice: Be fully yourself; it's what draws people.
cards.person: Sunny, bold, sociable, self-assured; a natural leader with a big heart and a quick temper.
cards.picture: A queen sits on a throne carved with lions, a sunflower in one hand and a wand in the other, a black cat seated at her feet.
cards.question: Where am I dimming myself to fit in?
cards.cat: Look, she has a black cat. Obviously the best card. Be her.
cards.name: Queen of Wands

names.golden_dawn: The Queen of the Thrones of Flame

cards.upright: The visionary leader. The King of Wands sees the big picture and inspires others to build it. Bold, honourable, entrepreneurial; take the lead and set the direction.
cards.reversed: Vision becomes domination. Impulsiveness, arrogance, impossible standards, or a leader who forgets the people doing the work. Lead by example, not by force.
cards.love: A passionate, committed partner who leads; protective and proud.
cards.work: Leadership, founding a business, setting vision, taking charge.
cards.spirit: The prince of the chariot of fire; air of fire; will made into a mission.
cards.advice: Lead with vision, and let others share the fire.
cards.person: Charismatic, visionary, decisive, honest; a born leader who hates being told what to do.
cards.picture: A king sits on a throne decorated with lions and salamanders, holding a flowering wand, a small salamander at his feet.
cards.question: What vision am I ready to lead?
cards.cat: Big vision, big chair, big ego. Two out of three is fine.
cards.name: King of Wands

names.golden_dawn: The Prince of the Chariot of Fire

cards.upright: The heart overflows. The Ace of Cups is a new beginning in feeling: love, compassion, creative inspiration, a spiritual opening. Let it pour; there is more where it came from.
cards.reversed: The cup is full but corked. Feelings held down, love blocked or withheld, or an emptiness that needs filling from inside first. Start by being kind to yourself.
cards.love: New love, deep feeling, a fresh start between partners.
cards.work: Creative inspiration, work that feeds the soul, good relationships with colleagues.
cards.spirit: The root of the powers of water; grace descending, the holy cup.
cards.advice: Open your heart and let it fill.
cards.picture: A hand from a cloud holds out an overflowing cup; five streams pour from it into a lily pond, and a white dove descends with a wafer into the cup.
cards.question: Where is my heart asking to be opened?
cards.cat: Your cup runneth over. Mop it up before you get sentimental at me.
cards.name: Ace of Cups

names.golden_dawn: The Root of the Powers of Water

cards.number_meaning: the seed: the whole force of the suit before it takes any shape
cards.rules: A quadrant of the heavens around the North Pole, over Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius (shared with the Princess of the suit)

cards.upright: Two cups raised to each other. The Two of Cups is mutual love and respect: a meeting of equals, a pledge, a reconciliation, a partnership where both give and receive. Something real is between you.
cards.reversed: The toast is uneven. An imbalance of feeling, a falling out, poor communication, or a bond that has drifted. It can also point back to the relationship you have with yourself.
cards.love: Mutual attraction, a new couple, commitment, a soulmate meeting.
cards.work: A strong partnership, a good deal, collaboration based on trust.
cards.spirit: The lord of love; Venus in Cancer; the two halves recognising each other.
cards.advice: Meet them as an equal.
cards.picture: A young man and woman face each other and exchange cups; above them rises a winged lion's head over a staff wound by two serpents.
cards.question: What do I bring to this bond, and what do I receive?
cards.cat: Two cups clinking. Adorable. Don't propose until you've seen them hungry.
cards.name: Two of Cups

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Love

cards.number_meaning: the first polarity: a choice, a meeting, a balance being found

keywords_reversed: the party that went too far
cards.upright: Raise a glass with your people. The Three of Cups is friendship, celebration and shared joy: reunions, parties, support from your circle. Happiness multiplied by company.
cards.reversed: Too much of a good thing, or the circle cracks. Overindulgence, gossip, a third person stirring trouble, or feeling left out. Find out who your real friends are.
cards.love: Celebrating love with friends; or a third party entering the picture.
cards.work: Teamwork, collaboration, celebrating a shared success.
cards.spirit: The lord of abundance; Mercury in Cancer; joy as a form of prayer.
cards.advice: Celebrate with the people who love you.
cards.picture: Three young women dance in a circle in a garden of harvest fruit, raising their cups to one another.
cards.question: Who are my people, and when did I last celebrate with them?
cards.cat: Party with your friends. Bring me back something. Tuna, preferably.
cards.name: Three of Cups

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Abundance

cards.number_meaning: the first form: growth, creation, something born from two

cards.upright: Three cups on the grass and a fourth offered from a cloud, and you don't look up. The Four of Cups is boredom, discontent, turning inward. Reflection has its place, but make sure you aren't ignoring a gift.
cards.reversed: You look up at last. Motivation returns, you accept what's offered, you stop sulking and start choosing. Or a deeper withdrawal; check which.
cards.love: Boredom or emotional distance; overlooking someone who cares.
cards.work: Lack of motivation, a stale job, an opportunity you're too jaded to see.
cards.spirit: The lord of blended pleasure; the Moon in Cancer; pleasure that has gone flat.
cards.advice: Look up. Something is being offered.
cards.picture: A young man sits under a tree with arms crossed, staring at three cups on the grass while a hand from a cloud offers him a fourth.
cards.question: What am I refusing to notice?
cards.cat: Someone's handing you a cup and you're sulking under a tree. Iconic.
cards.name: Four of Cups

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Blended Pleasure

cards.number_meaning: structure and rest: stability that can turn into stagnation

cards.upright: Three cups spilled, two still standing behind you. The Five of Cups is loss and the grief that follows: regret, disappointment, mourning what didn't work. The grief is real; so are the cups you haven't turned to see.
cards.reversed: Turning around. Acceptance, forgiveness, finding what remains, crossing the bridge home. The sorrow lifts enough to move again.
cards.love: Heartbreak, regret over a relationship, mourning what might have been.
cards.work: A setback or loss, a disappointing result, learning from failure.
cards.spirit: The lord of loss in pleasure; Mars in Scorpio; grief as a teacher.
cards.advice: Grieve what fell, then turn and see what's still standing.
cards.picture: A cloaked figure in black stands with head bowed over three spilled cups; two full cups stand behind, and a bridge crosses a river to a house.
cards.question: What am I grieving, and what is still here?
cards.cat: Three spilled, two left. You're crying at the wrong cups. Turn around.
cards.name: Five of Cups

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Loss in Pleasure

cards.number_meaning: disruption: conflict, loss or challenge that breaks the rut

cards.upright: Flowers in a cup, handed from one child to another. The Six of Cups is memory and innocence: nostalgia, childhood places, old friends returning, simple kindness. Let the past feed you without trapping you.
cards.reversed: Living in yesterday. Idealising the past, refusing to grow up, or old patterns repeating. Or the turn the other way: leaving the old home behind at last.
cards.love: An old flame, a sweet and innocent love, a childhood sweetheart.
cards.work: Returning to old work or skills; kindness among colleagues; working with children.
cards.spirit: The lord of pleasure; the Sun in Scorpio; the inner child remembered.
cards.advice: Honour the past, then bring its sweetness into now.
cards.picture: In an old courtyard a child offers a cup filled with white flowers to a smaller child; more cups of flowers stand around them, and a guard walks away in the background.
cards.question: What memory still holds a gift for me?
cards.cat: Nostalgia. Remember when you were tiny and less annoying? Me neither.
cards.name: Six of Cups

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Pleasure

cards.number_meaning: harmony restored: the heart of the suit, success, generosity

cards.upright: Seven cups floating in the clouds, each holding a different dream. The Seven of Cups is imagination and illusion: too many options, castles in the air, wishful thinking. Not every cup is real. Choose.
cards.reversed: The fog lifts. You see clearly which dream is worth chasing, or you decide at last. A welcome reality check.
cards.love: Fantasy and projection; too many options; idealising someone.
cards.work: Many possibilities, unclear direction, daydreaming instead of doing.
cards.spirit: The lord of illusionary success; Venus in Scorpio; the astral fog of glamour.
cards.advice: Pick one cup and look at it in daylight.
cards.picture: A dark figure faces seven cups floating in clouds, filled with a head, a veiled glowing figure, a serpent, a castle, jewels, a laurel wreath and a dragon.
cards.question: Which of my dreams is real, and which is decoration?
cards.cat: Seven fantasies and zero plans. Pick one. Not the dragon. Fine, the dragon.
cards.name: Seven of Cups

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Illusionary Success

cards.number_meaning: testing: courage, imagination, effort that has not yet paid

cards.upright: Turning your back on a stack of cups that no longer fills you. The Eight of Cups is the quiet departure: leaving something that looks fine for something truer. It takes courage to walk into the night for meaning.
cards.reversed: Afraid to go, or going without knowing why. Staying too long out of habit, drifting, or coming back to try again. Ask whether this is about the place or about you.
cards.love: Leaving a relationship that no longer feeds you; emotional withdrawal.
cards.work: Leaving a job, walking away from a project, looking for meaning over money.
cards.spirit: The lord of abandoned success; Saturn in Pisces; the pilgrim's departure.
cards.advice: Go, if your heart has already left.
cards.picture: Under a watching moon, a cloaked figure with a staff walks away from eight neatly stacked cups toward rocky hills.
cards.question: What have I outgrown that I'm still standing next to?
cards.cat: Walking out at night. Dramatic. Don't forget your keys, wanderer.
cards.name: Eight of Cups

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Abandoned Success

cards.number_meaning: movement and method: skill, speed, patterns, the mind at work

cards.upright: The wish card. The Nine of Cups is contentment and fulfilment: getting what you wanted and enjoying it. Comfort, pleasure, satisfaction. Make a wish; this card says yes.
