cards.reversed: Satisfaction that doesn't satisfy. Smugness, overindulgence, or wishes not quite granted. Or the inner turn: happiness you must find inside rather than in what you own.
cards.love: Contentment, a wish come true, emotional satisfaction.
cards.work: Achievement, success, recognition, things going your way.
cards.spirit: The lord of material happiness; Jupiter in Pisces; gratitude as a doorway.
cards.advice: Make the wish, and say thank you.
cards.picture: A well-fed man sits on a bench with arms crossed and a satisfied smile; behind him nine cups stand in an arc on a table draped in blue.
cards.question: What have I wished for that already came true?
cards.cat: The wish card. Congratulations. Don't wish for something dumb.
cards.name: Nine of Cups

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Material Happiness

cards.number_meaning: the near-peak: the suit at full intensity, for better or worse

cards.upright: The rainbow over the home. The Ten of Cups is emotional fulfilment: family, love, harmony, the happy ending. The peace of belonging somewhere with someone.
cards.reversed: The picture isn't matching the reality. Family tension, values out of step, or chasing an ideal no real family could live up to. Look at what is actually here.
cards.love: Lasting love, commitment, a happy family life.
cards.work: A workplace that feels like family; contentment in your role.
cards.spirit: The lord of perfected success; Mars in Pisces; the heart's kingdom complete.
cards.advice: Cherish your people.
cards.picture: A couple stand with arms raised toward a rainbow of ten cups arching across the sky; two children dance beside them, and a house sits on the hill beyond.
cards.question: What does home really mean to me?
cards.cat: Rainbow, family, happy house. Disgusting. I'm very happy for you.
cards.name: Ten of Cups

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Perfected Success

cards.number_meaning: the end of the cycle: the suit fully made real, completion or overload

cards.upright: A fish leaps out of the cup and the Page is delighted. The Page of Cups brings gentle surprises: an intuitive nudge, a creative idea, a tender message. Be open, playful and a little dreamy.
cards.reversed: Feelings too big for the cup. Emotional immaturity, sulking, creative blocks, or escaping into fantasy. Let the inner child speak, then answer as the grown-up.
cards.love: A sweet confession, a crush, a gentle new feeling.
cards.work: A creative opportunity, an artistic start, intuition guiding work.
cards.spirit: The princess of the waters; earth of water; the psychic first step.
cards.advice: Let yourself be surprised.
cards.person: A sensitive, imaginative young person or a dreamer; kind, intuitive, artistic, easily hurt.
cards.picture: A young person in a tunic printed with lotuses stands by the sea, holding a cup from which a small fish peeks out.
cards.question: What tender message am I receiving right now?
cards.cat: There's a fish in your cup. You're delighted. I'm hungry.
cards.name: Page of Cups

names.golden_dawn: The Princess of the Waters; the Lotus of the Palace of the Floods

court.rules: A quadrant of the heavens around the North Pole, over Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius

cards.upright: The romantic arrives on a slow white horse, cup held out. The Knight of Cups follows the heart: offers, invitations, romance, beauty, ideals. Accept the cup if it's sincere.
cards.reversed: Charm that doesn't deliver. Moodiness, idealism that collapses on contact with reality, or someone saying lovely things and doing nothing. Check the cup for a bottom.
cards.love: A romantic proposal, a courtship, a gesture from the heart.
cards.work: A creative offer, an artistic venture, work led by passion.
cards.spirit: The lord of the waves and the waters; fire of water; the grail quest.
cards.advice: Follow your heart, and bring your feet with you.
cards.person: A charming, romantic, idealistic person; artistic, gentle, sometimes moody and hard to pin to the ground.
cards.picture: A knight in shining armour with wings on his helmet rides a slow white horse toward a stream, holding out a cup as if making an offering.
cards.question: What does my heart want me to pursue?
cards.cat: Poetry on horseback. Very nice. Ask if he has a job.
cards.name: Knight of Cups

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of the Waves and the Waters; the King of the Hosts of the Sea

cards.upright: She sits at the water's edge holding a closed, ornate cup, reading what others can't see. The Queen of Cups is compassion and intuition with deep emotional wisdom. Feel fully, care deeply, keep your own shore.
cards.reversed: Drowning in feeling. Taking on everyone's pain, losing yourself in others, moods that rule the day. Care for yourself with the tenderness you give away.
cards.love: A loving, nurturing partner; emotional depth; intuitive connection.
cards.work: Counselling, caring roles, creative work; emotional intelligence at work.
cards.spirit: The queen of the thrones of the waters; water of water; the seer.
cards.advice: Trust what you feel, and keep a boundary.
cards.person: Empathic, intuitive, gentle, deeply caring; a healer of hearts who feels everything.
cards.picture: A queen sits on a throne carved with water spirits at the edge of the sea, gazing into an ornate covered cup she holds with both hands.
cards.question: Whose feelings am I carrying, and are they mine?
cards.cat: You feel everything. Pass some to me. No, wait. Keep them.
cards.name: Queen of Cups

names.golden_dawn: The Queen of the Thrones of the Waters

cards.upright: Calm on a throne floating on rough water. The King of Cups has mastered his feelings without denying them: diplomatic, wise, generous, steady. Keep your heart open and your head clear.
cards.reversed: The sea comes over the throne. Repression, mood swings, coldness, or feelings used to manipulate. Feel it honestly before it controls you.
cards.love: A mature, devoted partner; emotional stability.
cards.work: Leadership with empathy, mediation, diplomacy, the arts.
cards.spirit: The prince of the chariot of the waters; air of water; feeling ruled by wisdom.
cards.advice: Stay calm and kind under pressure.
cards.person: Kind, wise, diplomatic, emotionally steady; the counsellor everyone calls in a storm.
cards.picture: A king on a stone throne floats on a rough sea, a cup in one hand and a sceptre in the other, a fish pendant at his neck, a ship and a leaping fish behind.
cards.question: How do I stay steady when the water rises?
cards.cat: Calm as a lake, deep as a well. Also secretly sulking. I see you.
cards.name: King of Cups

names.golden_dawn: The Prince of the Chariot of the Waters

cards.upright: A sword held up through a crown. The Ace of Swords is the moment of clarity: a breakthrough, an idea that cuts through confusion, a truth spoken plainly. Use it to decide and to say what is real.
cards.reversed: The blade is dull or swung wildly. Confusion, mixed messages, a truth avoided, or words used to wound. Get the facts straight before you cut.
cards.love: Honest conversation, clarity about a relationship, a decision made.
cards.work: A sharp new idea, a breakthrough, clear strategy, a decisive move.
cards.spirit: The root of the powers of air; the sword of discernment that divides the true from the false.
cards.advice: Say the true thing clearly.
cards.picture: A hand from a cloud grips an upright double-edged sword whose tip passes through a gold crown hung with olive and palm, over bare grey mountains.
cards.question: What truth would set this free if I said it?
cards.cat: One clean cut. Try not to wave it around at dinner.
cards.name: Ace of Swords

names.golden_dawn: The Root of the Powers of Air

cards.number_meaning: the seed: the whole force of the suit before it takes any shape
cards.rules: A quadrant of the heavens around the North Pole, over Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces (shared with the Princess of the suit)

cards.upright: Blindfolded, swords crossed over the heart. The Two of Swords is a stalemate: a choice avoided, feelings held at arm's length, a truce that buys time. Peace for now, but the sea behind you keeps moving.
cards.reversed: The blindfold slips. New information forces a choice, or the pressure of deciding becomes overwhelming. Take it off and look.
cards.love: Avoiding a decision about a relationship; emotional stand-off.
cards.work: A difficult choice, deadlock in negotiation, stalling.
cards.spirit: The lord of peace restored; the Moon in Libra; the balanced mind before the cut.
cards.advice: Take off the blindfold and choose.
cards.picture: A blindfolded woman in white sits on a bench by the sea, arms crossed over her chest holding two long swords; a crescent moon hangs above and rocks rise from the water.
cards.question: What am I refusing to look at so I don't have to choose?
cards.cat: Blindfolded, holding two swords, by the sea. Bold look. Choose something.
cards.name: Two of Swords

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Peace Restored

cards.number_meaning: the first polarity: a choice, a meeting, a balance being found

cards.upright: Three swords through a heart in the rain. The Three of Swords is heartbreak and sorrow, often from a painful truth: a betrayal, a parting, words that cut. It hurts because it matters. Let it rain.
cards.reversed: The storm passes. Forgiveness, release, mending, letting the swords come out one by one. Or sorrow held in too long; let it be felt.
cards.love: Heartbreak, separation, betrayal, a painful realisation.
cards.work: Disappointment, criticism, a setback that stings.
cards.spirit: The lord of sorrow; Saturn in Libra; the wound that opens the heart.
cards.advice: Feel it fully; it will pass.
cards.picture: A red heart pierced by three swords hangs against a grey sky of storm clouds and falling rain.
cards.question: What truth hurt me, and what did it teach?
cards.cat: Ouch. Your heart's a pincushion. Cry, eat something, then text nobody.
cards.name: Three of Swords

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Sorrow

cards.number_meaning: the first form: growth, creation, something born from two

cards.upright: Lying still in a quiet chapel. The Four of Swords is rest after strife: retreat, contemplation, getting your strength back. Step away and let the mind fall silent.
cards.reversed: Rest refused or rest overdue. Restlessness, burnout, rushing back too soon, or stagnation dressed up as rest. Your energy needs to come back first.
cards.love: Time apart, a pause in the relationship, space to think.
cards.work: A break, a sabbatical, stepping back before the next push.
cards.spirit: The lord of rest from strife; Jupiter in Libra; the meditation hall.
cards.advice: Rest now; the fight can wait.
cards.picture: The stone effigy of a knight lies on a tomb with hands joined in prayer; one sword lies along the tomb and three hang on the wall beneath a stained-glass window.
cards.question: What would real rest look like for me right now?
cards.cat: Lie down. You've been talking for days. I've been lying down for years. Join me.
cards.name: Four of Swords

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Rest from Strife

cards.number_meaning: structure and rest: stability that can turn into stagnation

cards.upright: One man gathers the swords while two walk away defeated. The Five of Swords is conflict where nobody really wins: hostility, humiliation, a victory that costs more than it gains. Ask whether this fight is worth it.
cards.reversed: The war winds down. Making amends, letting old resentments go, or the sting of regret afterwards. Peace is possible if someone puts down the swords.
cards.love: Arguments, hurtful words, a power struggle, someone needing to be right.
cards.work: Office conflict, unfair tactics, a hollow win.
cards.spirit: The lord of defeat; Venus in Aquarius; the ego's war.
cards.advice: Choose peace over being right.
cards.picture: A smirking young man holds three swords and looks at two more on the ground, while two figures walk away toward a stormy shore, one with face in hands.
cards.question: Is winning this worth what it costs?
cards.cat: You won the argument. Everyone left. Enjoy your swords.
cards.name: Five of Swords

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Defeat

cards.number_meaning: disruption: conflict, loss or challenge that breaks the rut

cards.upright: A ferry carries the passengers across to the calmer shore. The Six of Swords is transition: leaving difficulty behind, moving on, slowly getting somewhere better. It is quiet, sad and hopeful at once.
cards.reversed: The boat stalls. Resisting change, carrying too much baggage, or unfinished business pulling you back. Decide what can stay on this shore.
cards.love: Moving on from a hard relationship; travelling together through change.
cards.work: A transfer, a move, leaving a difficult job.
cards.spirit: The lord of earned success; Mercury in Aquarius; the crossing of the waters.
cards.advice: Keep going; the water gets calmer.
cards.picture: A ferryman poles a flat boat toward a far shore; a cloaked woman and a child sit inside with six swords standing upright in the boat. The water is rough on one side and smooth on the other.
cards.question: What am I carrying across that I could leave behind?
cards.cat: You're finally leaving. Good. Don't take all six swords, they'll sink the boat.
cards.name: Six of Swords

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Earned Success

cards.number_meaning: harmony restored: the heart of the suit, success, generosity

cards.upright: Tiptoeing away with five swords. The Seven of Swords is cunning and stealth: strategy, secrets, someone getting away with something, or you going it alone. Be clever, and be honest with yourself about the cost.
cards.reversed: The trick is revealed. Confession, a guilty conscience, being found out, or giving back what was taken. Or the deepest lie: the one told to yourself.
cards.love: Secrets, dishonesty, a partner not telling the whole story.
cards.work: Office politics, strategy, someone taking credit, a plan kept close.
cards.spirit: The lord of unstable effort; the Moon in Aquarius; the trickster's path.
cards.advice: Be smart, not sneaky.
cards.picture: A man creeps away from a camp of tents, carrying five swords and grinning back over his shoulder; two swords stay stuck in the ground behind him.
cards.question: Where am I not being fully honest, even with myself?
cards.cat: Sneaking off with swords. Subtle. You're grinning. That's how they always catch you.
cards.name: Seven of Swords

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Unstable Effort

cards.number_meaning: testing: courage, imagination, effort that has not yet paid

cards.upright: Bound, blindfolded and surrounded by swords, but the swords aren't touching her and her feet are free. The Eight of Swords is the trap made of thought: limits you believe in, fear that keeps you still. You can walk out.
cards.reversed: The bindings loosen. You see how the trap worked and step out of it, or you begin to. Freedom starts with a different thought.
cards.love: Feeling stuck in a relationship; fear of leaving or of being seen.
cards.work: Feeling trapped in a job; limiting beliefs about what you can do.
cards.spirit: The lord of shortened force; Jupiter in Gemini; the prison of the mind.
cards.advice: Take one step. The swords won't stop you.
cards.picture: A blindfolded woman, loosely bound, stands in shallow mud surrounded by eight swords planted in the ground, a castle on the hill behind her.
cards.question: What story about myself is keeping me stuck?
cards.cat: You're tied up with string surrounded by sticks. Walk. I'll wait.
cards.name: Eight of Swords

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Shortened Force

cards.number_meaning: movement and method: skill, speed, patterns, the mind at work

cards.upright: Awake in the dark with your head in your hands. The Nine of Swords is worry and anguish, fear that is worst in the small hours, guilt that loops. The swords are on the wall, not in you; the mind is doing most of the cutting.
cards.reversed: The night begins to end. Reaching out, telling someone, seeing that the worst fears were bigger in the dark. Or a worry kept too secret for too long; bring it into daylight.
cards.love: Anxiety about a relationship; guilt; fear of losing someone.
cards.work: Stress, worrying about work, fear of failure.
cards.spirit: The lord of despair and cruelty; Mars in Gemini; the dark night of the mind.
cards.advice: Tell someone. Morning comes.
cards.picture: A woman sits up in bed in the dark with her face in her hands; nine swords hang in a row on the black wall behind her, and her quilt is patterned with roses and the signs of the zodiac.
cards.question: Which of my fears are real, and which are the night talking?
cards.cat: Up at 3 a.m. again, doom-scrolling your own brain. Put the phone down. Pet a cat.
cards.name: Nine of Swords

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Despair and Cruelty

cards.number_meaning: the near-peak: the suit at full intensity, for better or worse

cards.upright: Ten swords, and the sky cracking into dawn behind them. The Ten of Swords is the very end of a painful situation: rock bottom, betrayal, the moment it can't get worse. And so it gets better from here.
cards.reversed: Getting up off the ground. Regeneration, the slow mending after a defeat, the lesson learned. Or refusing to admit something is over, which keeps the swords in.
cards.love: A painful break-up, betrayal, the end of a relationship.
cards.work: A collapse, a project ending, being let go; a hard ending that clears the ground.
cards.spirit: The lord of ruin; the Sun in Gemini; the end of the night, the first light of day.
cards.advice: Let it be over. The sun is coming up.
cards.picture: A man lies face down by still water with ten swords in his back and a red cloth over him; the black sky above breaks into a band of yellow dawn over distant hills.
cards.question: What is truly finished, and what dawn is behind it?
cards.cat: Ten swords. A bit much, honestly. Get up, the sun's coming. So am I, for breakfast.
cards.name: Ten of Swords

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Ruin

cards.number_meaning: the end of the cycle: the suit fully made real, completion or overload

cards.upright: Sword raised, hair in the wind, watching everything. The Page of Swords is the curious mind: questions, new ideas, alertness, a hunger for truth. Learn, ask, and speak carefully.
cards.reversed: Words outrun the thinking. Gossip, spying, sharp remarks, ideas never finished. Think before you cut.
cards.love: Testing the water with words; mixed signals; honest questions.
cards.work: Research, learning, new ideas, careful observation.
cards.spirit: The princess of the rushing winds; earth of air; the mind waking up.
cards.advice: Ask the question, then listen to the answer.
cards.person: A quick, curious, talkative young person or a student; clever, restless, sometimes sharp-tongued.
cards.picture: A young person stands on rough, windy ground with clouds racing behind, holding a sword upright with both hands and looking sharply to one side.
cards.question: What am I curious about, and what am I suspicious of?
cards.cat: Lots of questions. Some are good. Most are just you being nosy.
cards.name: Page of Swords

names.golden_dawn: The Princess of the Rushing Winds; the Lotus of the Palace of Air

court.rules: A quadrant of the heavens around the North Pole, over Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces

cards.upright: Galloping into the wind, sword first. The Knight of Swords is fast, bold action driven by an idea: ambition, determination, speed. Move decisively, and look where you're charging.
cards.reversed: Speed without direction. Aggression, harsh words, recklessness, plans abandoned at full gallop. Slow the horse and aim.
cards.love: A fast-moving romance; or a partner who charges in and says too much.
cards.work: Drive, ambition, a rapid push, competition, decisive action.
cards.spirit: The lord of the winds and the breezes; fire of air; thought becoming action.
cards.advice: Act fast, and think one step ahead.
cards.person: Quick-witted, ambitious, assertive, blunt; brilliant in a crisis and exhausting at dinner.
cards.picture: A knight charges at full speed into a strong wind on a white horse, sword raised; trees bend and clouds tear behind him.
cards.question: What am I rushing at, and have I aimed?
cards.cat: Charging into a headwind, yelling. Very you. Mind the trees.
cards.name: Knight of Swords

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of the Winds and the Breezes; the King of the Spirits of Air

cards.upright: She sits above the clouds, sword upright, one hand open. The Queen of Swords is clear sight and honest speech: boundaries, independence, wisdom earned through pain. She sees through everything, and says so kindly.
cards.reversed: The sword turns cold. Bitterness, harsh judgement, isolation, or truth used as a weapon. Soften the blade without losing its edge.
cards.love: Clear communication, independence within love, boundaries that protect.
cards.work: Clear thinking, honest feedback, editing, analysis, leadership through clarity.
cards.spirit: The queen of the thrones of air; water of air; the clear-eyed widow of the mysteries.
cards.advice: Be clear, be honest, be kind.
cards.person: Sharp, perceptive, independent, honest, often someone who has come through grief; no time for nonsense.
cards.picture: A queen sits in profile on a throne carved with butterflies and a winged head, sword raised upright in one hand, the other hand held open, above a bank of clouds; a single bird flies high above.
cards.question: Where do I need to speak plainly?
cards.cat: She sees straight through you. So do I. You're not that complicated.
cards.name: Queen of Swords

names.golden_dawn: The Queen of the Thrones of Air

cards.upright: The judge, calm and upright, sword slightly tilted. The King of Swords is intellectual authority: truth, ethics, sound judgement, clear thinking. Decide by reason and principle.
cards.reversed: Power used without heart. Manipulation, cold logic, cruelty, or rules enforced to control. Bring the heart back into the judgement.
cards.love: A mature, rational partner; a relationship that values honesty over romance.
cards.work: Leadership through expertise; legal matters; strategy; clear decisions.
cards.spirit: The prince of the chariot of the winds; air of air; the sovereign mind.
cards.advice: Decide by truth, and say it with care.
cards.person: Rational, principled, articulate, authoritative; a judge, expert or strategist; fair but distant.
cards.picture: A king sits on a high throne carved with butterflies and crescents, holding an upright sword slightly tilted, under a sky of drifting clouds and birds.
cards.question: What would a fair, clear-headed judge say about this?
cards.cat: Very logical. Very fair. Very boring at parties. I respect it.
cards.name: King of Swords

names.golden_dawn: The Prince of the Chariot of the Winds

cards.upright: A golden coin held out from the cloud over a garden. The Ace of Pentacles is a real, material beginning: a job offer, money, a property, a seed that can grow into lasting wealth. Plant it in good soil.
cards.reversed: The coin slips through the fingers. A missed opportunity, poor planning, or worry about scarcity driving bad choices. Build the foundation before you build the house.
cards.love: A grounded, real start; commitment you can build on.
cards.work: A new job, a business opportunity, a raise, financial beginnings.
cards.spirit: The root of the powers of earth; spirit made solid; the gate through the garden.
cards.advice: Take the opportunity and plant it.
cards.picture: A hand from a cloud holds out a golden pentacle over a garden of lilies; a path runs through an arch of hedge roses toward distant mountains.
cards.question: What real, solid opportunity is in front of me?
cards.cat: Someone's handing you money. Take it. Don't buy anything shiny with it.
cards.name: Ace of Pentacles

names.golden_dawn: The Root of the Powers of Earth

cards.number_meaning: the seed: the whole force of the suit before it takes any shape
cards.rules: A quadrant of the heavens around the North Pole, over Aries, Taurus, Gemini (shared with the Princess of the suit)

cards.upright: Dancing with two coins in a loop of infinity while ships ride the waves behind. The Two of Pentacles is juggling: balancing priorities, adapting, keeping several things in motion with good humour. You can handle it.
cards.reversed: One too many balls in the air. Overwhelm, financial juggling, overcommitment, chaos. Put something down before everything drops.
cards.love: Balancing a relationship with everything else; a playful, flexible bond.
cards.work: Multitasking, managing several projects, adapting to changing demands.
cards.spirit: The lord of harmonious change; Jupiter in Capricorn; the dance of the opposites.
cards.advice: Keep your rhythm and drop what doesn't matter.
cards.picture: A young man in a tall hat dances while juggling two pentacles joined by a loop shaped like the sign of infinity; behind him two ships rise and fall on high waves.
cards.question: What am I juggling, and what can I put down?
cards.cat: Juggling. Cute. Who taught you that? Nobody. It shows.
cards.name: Two of Pentacles

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Harmonious Change

cards.number_meaning: the first polarity: a choice, a meeting, a balance being found

cards.upright: The craftsman on the bench, the monk and the architect with the plans. The Three of Pentacles is good work done together: skill, collaboration, recognition from people who know. Build it well, with others.
cards.reversed: The team pulls in different directions. Poor workmanship, ignoring expertise, or trying to do it all alone. Get the plan straight and listen to the builder.
cards.love: Building a relationship together, working as a team.
cards.work: Collaboration, skilled work, apprenticeship, being recognised for quality.
cards.spirit: The lord of material works; Mars in Capricorn; the temple raised by many hands.
cards.advice: Bring the right people and build it properly.
cards.picture: A stonemason stands on a bench in a church archway carving the stone, while a monk and a figure holding plans look up and consult with him.
cards.question: Who do I need to build this with?
cards.cat: Teamwork. Groan. Fine. Let the person who knows what they're doing do it.
cards.name: Three of Pentacles

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Material Works

cards.number_meaning: the first form: growth, creation, something born from two

cards.upright: A coin on the head, a coin held to the chest, a coin under each foot. The Four of Pentacles is security and control: saving, holding on, protecting what you have. Safe, yes. But a closed hand can't receive.
cards.reversed: The grip loosens, wisely or not. Letting go and becoming generous, or the opposite: greed tightening, or money running out. Find a middle between hoarding and spilling.
cards.love: Possessiveness, holding on too tightly, emotional guardedness.
cards.work: Financial caution, saving, controlling budgets, resistance to change.
cards.spirit: The lord of earthly power; the Sun in Capricorn; the miser and the steward.
cards.advice: Keep what's yours, and open your hand a little.
cards.picture: A crowned man sits on a stool clutching a pentacle to his chest, another balanced on his crown and one under each foot, a city behind him.
cards.question: What am I holding so tightly that nothing new can reach me?
cards.cat: Hugging your coins like a dragon. Relax. Nobody wants your loose change.
cards.name: Four of Pentacles

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Earthly Power

cards.number_meaning: structure and rest: stability that can turn into stagnation

cards.upright: Two figures in the snow pass a lit church window without looking up. The Five of Pentacles is hard times: money worries, feeling shut out, alone in the cold. Help is closer than it seems.
cards.reversed: Coming in from the cold. The worst of a hard time ends, help arrives, or you finally accept it. Things begin to warm.
cards.love: Feeling left out or unloved; going through hardship together.
cards.work: Financial strain, job loss, insecurity; reach for the help on offer.
cards.spirit: The lord of material trouble; Mercury in Taurus; the poverty that teaches what matters.
cards.advice: Look up and ask for help.
cards.picture: Two ragged figures, one on crutches, trudge through falling snow past a lit stained-glass window showing five pentacles.
cards.question: Where is help being offered that I haven't seen?
cards.cat: You're standing in the snow next to an open door. Go in. Honestly.
cards.name: Five of Pentacles

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Material Trouble

cards.number_meaning: disruption: conflict, loss or challenge that breaks the rut

cards.upright: A merchant with scales drops coins into open hands. The Six of Pentacles is generosity and balance: giving, receiving, sharing what you have. Notice which side you're on, and that both are blessed.
cards.reversed: The scales tip. Gifts with strings, debts, charity that keeps someone small, or giving so much you have nothing left. Make the exchange fair.
cards.love: Balanced give and take; or one partner always giving.
cards.work: Fair pay, investment, loans, mentoring, charity work.
cards.spirit: The lord of material success; the Moon in Taurus; the circulation of grace.
cards.advice: Give freely, receive gracefully, keep the scales level.
cards.picture: A well-dressed merchant holding scales gives coins to one of two kneeling beggars, six pentacles floating above them.
cards.question: Where do I give, and where do I let myself receive?
cards.cat: Giving money away. Generous. Keep a little for my treats.
cards.name: Six of Pentacles

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Material Success

cards.number_meaning: harmony restored: the heart of the suit, success, generosity

cards.upright: Leaning on the hoe, looking at the crop. The Seven of Pentacles is patience and assessment: you've worked, and it's growing, but harvest isn't today. Take stock and decide what to keep tending.
cards.reversed: The crop isn't paying off, or you're tired of waiting. Impatience, poor returns, or effort put into the wrong field. Reassess before you either quit or double down.
cards.love: A relationship that needs time; asking whether it's worth the effort.
cards.work: A long-term project, investment, waiting for results.
cards.spirit: The lord of success unfulfilled; Saturn in Taurus; the slow seasons of the soul.
cards.advice: Be patient, and weed what isn't growing.
cards.picture: A young farmer leans on his hoe and studies seven pentacles growing on a green vine.
cards.question: What have I planted, and is it worth more waiting?
cards.cat: Staring at your plant won't make it grow. I've tried. With the fridge.
cards.name: Seven of Pentacles

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Success Unfulfilled

cards.number_meaning: testing: courage, imagination, effort that has not yet paid

cards.upright: Hammering pentacles one after another at the bench. The Eight of Pentacles is diligent work and growing mastery: practice, apprenticeship, quality, focus. Keep at it; each one gets better.
cards.reversed: The work loses its soul or its standard. Perfectionism, careless shortcuts, repetitive work with no meaning, or skill unused. Find the reason you started.
cards.love: Working on a relationship; dedication shown in small, reliable things.
cards.work: Skill-building, training, a craft, quality work, dedication.
cards.spirit: The lord of prudence; the Sun in Virgo; devotion through work.
cards.advice: Practise, and take pride in the craft.
cards.picture: A craftsman sits at a bench carving a pentacle; six finished pentacles hang on a post beside him and one lies at his feet, a town in the distance.
cards.question: What skill am I willing to practise until it's mastered?
cards.cat: Doing the same thing eight times. Diligent. Or stuck. Let's say diligent.
cards.name: Eight of Pentacles

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Prudence

cards.number_meaning: movement and method: skill, speed, patterns, the mind at work

cards.upright: Alone in her vineyard with a falcon on her glove. The Nine of Pentacles is the reward of discipline: independence, comfort, financial security, the pleasure of a life you built yourself. Enjoy it.
cards.reversed: The garden walls feel lonely, or the luxury is borrowed. Overwork, dependence on others, showing off, or spending more than you have. True security is self-respect.
cards.love: Self-love and independence; a partner who complements rather than completes you.
cards.work: Financial independence, reward for effort, self-employment.
cards.spirit: The lord of material gain; Venus in Virgo; the tamed falcon of the mind.
cards.advice: Enjoy what you've earned.
cards.picture: A richly dressed woman stands in a vineyard heavy with grapes, a hooded falcon on her gloved hand, nine pentacles growing among the vines, a manor behind.
cards.question: What have I built for myself that I can now enjoy?
cards.cat: Garden, falcon, wine. Fancy. I'd eat the falcon.
cards.name: Nine of Pentacles

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Material Gain

cards.number_meaning: the near-peak: the suit at full intensity, for better or worse

cards.upright: Three generations and their dogs under the family arch. The Ten of Pentacles is lasting wealth and legacy: family, inheritance, roots, security that outlasts one life. Build what will remain.
cards.reversed: The legacy is shaken. Family disputes, money troubles, an inheritance fought over, or a break with tradition. Ask what you want to pass on.
cards.love: A lasting commitment, family, building a shared future.
cards.work: Long-term success, a family business, a pension, lasting wealth.
cards.spirit: The lord of wealth; Mercury in Virgo; the ten spheres made into a kingdom.
cards.advice: Think in generations.
cards.picture: An old man in a patterned robe sits under an archway with two dogs; a couple and a child stand nearby, and ten pentacles are laid over the scene in the shape of the Tree of Life.
cards.question: What do I want to leave behind me?
cards.cat: Family, money, dogs. Ugh, dogs. Still a good card.
cards.name: Ten of Pentacles

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of Wealth

cards.number_meaning: the end of the cycle: the suit fully made real, completion or overload

cards.upright: Holding up a coin and studying it like a mystery. The Page of Pentacles is the careful student: new skills, practical opportunities, steady ambition. Learn, plan, start small and real.
cards.reversed: All plan, no progress. Procrastination, unrealistic goals, distraction. Put down the dream board and do the first practical thing.
cards.love: A slow, careful start; showing love through practical things.
cards.work: A new course, an apprenticeship, a job offer, starting a business carefully.
cards.spirit: The princess of the echoing hills; earth of earth; the deep stillness of the seed before the harvest.
cards.advice: Study it, then make a start.
cards.person: A studious, practical, patient young person or beginner; reliable, curious about how things work.
cards.picture: A young person stands in a green field with flowers, holding up a pentacle in both hands and gazing at it intently, ploughed land and trees behind.
cards.question: What do I want to learn properly?
cards.cat: Staring at a coin like it holds secrets. It might. Mostly it holds a coin.
cards.name: Page of Pentacles

names.golden_dawn: The Princess of the Echoing Hills; the Rose of the Palace of Earth

court.rules: A quadrant of the heavens around the North Pole, over Aries, Taurus, Gemini

cards.upright: The only knight standing still. The Knight of Pentacles is slow, steady, reliable work: routine, method, patience, finishing what you start. Not exciting, and it gets there.
cards.reversed: The rut. Boredom, stubbornness, overwork with no joy, or perfectionism that never ships. Change the routine before it changes you.
cards.love: A loyal, steady partner; a slow-burning, dependable bond.
cards.work: Diligence, routine, careful progress, a long project done properly.
cards.spirit: The lord of the wide and fertile land; fire of earth; the ploughman's faith.
cards.advice: Keep the steady pace.
cards.person: Dependable, patient, methodical, loyal; slow to warm, slower to quit.
cards.picture: A knight in dark armour sits on a heavy black horse that stands still in a ploughed field, holding a pentacle and looking at it.
cards.question: What am I building slowly, and is it still worth it?
cards.cat: Your horse isn't moving. Neither are you. Both of you are proud of it.
cards.name: Knight of Pentacles

names.golden_dawn: The Lord of the Wide and Fertile Land; the King of the Spirits of Earth

keywords_reversed: work and home out of balance
cards.upright: A queen in a garden, a coin in her lap, a rabbit at her feet. The Queen of Pentacles is practical love: nurturing, providing, making a warm, abundant home. Look after your world and your body in it.
cards.reversed: Giving everything and keeping nothing. Self-neglect, smothering, a home or work life out of balance, money worries. Tend your own garden too.
cards.love: A caring, nurturing partner; a cosy home life.
cards.work: Running a home business, care work, managing resources well.
cards.spirit: The queen of the thrones of earth; water of earth; the fertile mother of the world.
cards.advice: Take care of yourself as well as you take care of others.
cards.person: Warm, practical, generous, grounded; the one who feeds everybody and remembers birthdays.
cards.picture: A queen sits on a throne carved with fruit and goats in a garden of roses, cradling a pentacle in her lap; a rabbit sits in the grass nearby.
cards.question: How well am I caring for my own body and home?
cards.cat: She feeds everyone. Adopt her. I volunteer as the first child.
cards.name: Queen of Pentacles

names.golden_dawn: The Queen of the Thrones of Earth

cards.upright: The king in robes embroidered with grapes, throne carved with bulls. The King of Pentacles is material mastery: wealth, business sense, security, generous leadership. You've built a kingdom; run it well.
cards.reversed: The kingdom becomes a cage. Greed, stubbornness, obsession with status, or bad decisions with money. Wealth is a tool, not a crown.
cards.love: A stable, protective, generous partner.
cards.work: Business success, investment, leadership, financial security.
cards.spirit: The prince of the chariot of earth; air of earth; spirit at ease in matter.
cards.advice: Use your abundance wisely and well.
cards.person: Successful, reliable, generous, grounded; a provider and builder who likes nice things.
cards.picture: A king sits in a garden on a throne carved with bull heads, his robe covered in grapes and vines, holding a sceptre and a pentacle, his castle behind.
cards.question: What does real wealth mean to me?
cards.cat: Grape robe, bull throne, money. Peak dad energy. Fine. Respect.
cards.name: King of Pentacles

names.golden_dawn: The Prince of the Chariot of Earth

major-00+major-01.read: The leap meets the tools. A beginning you can actually pull off: the idea and the skill arrive together. Start now, and start properly.

major-00+major-02.read: Step forward on a hunch. The path isn't visible yet, but something quiet knows the way; trust the pull more than the map.

major-00+major-03.read: A fresh start that grows fast. Play, make things, let it flourish without a plan; plenty follows the open heart.

major-00+major-04.read: Freedom meets the rules. Either the wild idea needs a structure to survive, or the structure needs a breath of fresh air.

major-00+major-05.read: The beginner and the teacher. Learn the tradition before you break it, or step outside the old school and find your own way.

major-00+major-06.read: Falling for someone or something without a script. A choice made with the heart wide open; make sure it's really yours.

major-00+major-07.read: A journey begins at speed. Travel, a bold move, a launch; aim the energy or it scatters.

major-00+major-08.read: Innocent courage. You can calm what scares you by not taking it so seriously; a light hand holds the lion.

major-00+major-09.read: The start and the search. Set off alone, or step off the road for a while to find out where you really want to go.

major-00+major-10.read: Luck favours the leap. A chance appears out of nowhere; jump while the wheel is turning your way.

major-00+major-11.read: Freedom with consequences. Leap, but know the cost; read the small print before you sign up for the adventure.

major-00+major-12.read: The leap held in the air. Wait before you jump, or let go entirely and see the world upside down for a while.

major-00+major-13.read: A clean ending and a clean start. Something finishes so the road can open; walk on without looking back.

major-00+major-14.read: A gentle beginning. Go slowly and blend the new into your life; patience makes the leap land softly.

major-00+major-15.read: Freedom, or a trap that looks like freedom. Watch the reckless pleasure that quietly turns into a habit.
major-00+major-15.cat: Free as a bird. A bird in a very nice cage. Check the door.

major-00+major-16.read: The leap off the edge, or the floor giving way. A start nobody planned; you'll land somewhere new.

major-00+major-17.read: Hope with nothing to lose. A brave fresh start under a good sky; follow the light, it's real.

major-00+major-18.read: Walking in the dark. A step into the unknown with fears and mirages on the path; feel each step before you trust it.

major-00+major-19.read: The pure joy of starting. Childlike delight, an easy yes, a bright road; enjoy it while it's this simple.

major-00+major-20.read: A calling answered without overthinking. You hear the summons and say yes; a reborn sense of direction.

major-00+major-21.read: The end of one journey is the first step of the next. Completion, then the open road again.
major-00+major-21.cat: Finished one adventure, starting another. You never sit down, do you.

major-01+major-02.read: Action and intuition, outer and inner. What you know in silence you can now make real; use both hands.

major-01+major-03.read: Skill meets fertile ground. Creative work that takes root and grows; make something beautiful and useful.

major-01+major-04.read: Will with structure behind it. A plan with power: build the business, lead the project, make it official.

major-01+major-05.read: The maker and the teacher. Learn the craft properly, or teach what you can do; mastery through method.

major-01+major-06.read: Making a choice happen. Charm, attraction, a union you can actively shape; mean what you say.

major-01+major-07.read: Willpower in motion. Drive, focus and the skill to win; push forward and steer.

major-01+major-08.read: Power used gently. Skill with self-control; the strongest move here is the patient one.

major-01+major-09.read: Skill in private. Study, practise and refine alone before you show it; quiet mastery.

major-01+major-10.read: Seizing the moment. Luck turns and you're ready for it; act while the timing is right.

major-01+major-11.read: Skill used honestly. Contracts, negotiations, anything legal; make your case cleanly and it holds.

major-01+major-12.read: Will on pause. Stop pushing; the trick this time is to wait and see things from another side.
